Although it has promise, I cannot reccommend this game, and that is after playing literally thousands of hours of Eugen's wargame series. To be blunt, balance is a joke. The two key things that completely wreck balance are the fact that AA is near-worthless (you too can have 16 AA guns up, with a leader buffing them and shoot down zero planes!), and only ever stops the first plane in a train from hitting you by panicing it to retreat, letting every other plane pound you.
If the overwhelming effect of airpower isn't enough of an issue, the "improved" morale system will be. Everyone panics near-instantly. It is tooth gnashing to have guys throw grenades, and 37mm fire at your heavy tanks and they retreat under the hits, usually exposing their sides. Of course, having the command units around is supposed to help this, but nothing stops those command units from panicing themselves.
Finally, there are a bunch of little things - like them putting in instant kill crits (literally in terms of crew and ammo, effectively in bailing out - there is no way to recrew bailed vehicles for no apparent reason)... despite the fact that any hit (even bounces or totally ineffective fire) can cause a hit. I have seen first hand a Panther blow up to a 37mm hit frontally due to a crit. Eugen needs to make it so that not all hits have a crit chance.
The game systems are otherwise excellent, and it runs well enough. For all of the rest of the game being so good, I cannot reccommend an RTT (particularly a primarily PvP one) with such poor balance.

To start off, just wanted to point out that this is my first review so apologies if it won't be as in-depth as probably other reviews but I'll try my best. c:
This game was bought by me when this game was in a bundle with Breath of Death VII. The people who created a game decided to make a sale which was the lowest sale they have ever done on their games. That being said, I did purchase this game for €0.24 ($0.26 & £0.17) and I will make reference to it in the review.
You play as Cthulhu, a fictional deity created by H.P. Lovecraft in his story appropriately named: "Call of Cthulhu." In this game, Zeboyd Games (the creators) took a different approach for this character and with Cthulhu being basically the lord of insanity instead made it so that his powers have been relenquished and for him to obtain them back he must become a true hero which plots you into an epic quest in an open world where you meet characters to help you on your journey, dungeons to explore and towns to visit.
This game holds up and will hold up in the forseeing years to come and I only wish that Zeboyd Games would get more publicity with their games because they are quite good especially for those who love turn-based old-school RPGs. Heck, the only reason why I found out about this game was from it being a sale and it definitely needs much more publicity. I'd hate to see it stay an underrated great game. I loved the game and am now cordially introduced into the amazing developers that are Zeboyd Games and are excited to see the other additions they give out and their other titles.
This game receives a rating of:
for those familiar with the genre, especially the old-school RPGs.

for those who want to try a new RPG genre that can be compared to other RPGs and a starter to the genre. If you can get past the repetitive nature of the turn-based RPGs and enjoy the genre as well as the story, dialogue and soundtrack within this game then you will definitely enjoy it.
Thank you very much for reading my review, please give me feedback if any and happy gaming.

This game is in Early access. Thats normally a turn off for me, and I buy games based on what Im getting at the time I buy it as opposed to promises, but in this game, as it stands right now, this game easily has enough content to justify its 25 CAD/20 USD price tag (which apparently will never change or go on sale according to the devs).
This game is about optimization and micromanagement. If you dont like that, you wont like it. There isnt really any sort of visual element to building your bases/factories etc as pretty much all items are functional and affect the gameplay. There is a lot of tedious busy work even after setting up a nicely running factory, but thats kind of what you sign up for with a game like this. With tons of tech tree unlocks to research, then eventually farm materials for and manufacture, this is not a game youll be done with quickly and has quite a lot of content.
Campaign wise, so far, there is one major campaign which has a somewhat interesting story I suppose, but really focuses on teaching you the basics all the way through the campaign. Its not that its drawn out and unnecessary (Though it could be a  little shorter), but that this game has so many different Items, short cuts, systems to work with that to be competent, I think its a good idea to play through the campaign first.
That might seem weird, as if Im saying the campaign isnt where youll be spending most of your time, and thats because that is indeed the case. While the campaign is ok, and from a purely dollars to time point of view thats all fine and dandy, the core of this game is the freeplay mode where you can build out, try different scenarios from different seeds with different settings, with people, without people many different ways. Each one of these games lasts quite some time too. Much like minecraft, do not ever expect to be done with that world within an hour. It no typical mission and you can expect a game to last days of in game time.
Why does it last so long? the micro management. It really does start off slow, but when you start building off your factory things speed up somewhat. I personally feel that the pacing is a bit slow making you feel like youre doing more busy work than necessary especially at the start, but it does not kill the game. Unfortunately though, it does mean that often times, when you want to leave it sitting and running in the background, things can go awry quickly. Now, a lot of this is avoidable, probably simply by being better than I am, but I doubt you can completely escape this. The good news though is that even if thats not ideal for you, this game has great mod support, so you can change it to your liking.
Mod support is great. Though not on the steam workshop and through its own mod portal, modding is made easy with  an outlined frame work and drag and drop installations. On the modders side of things, it seems they put in the effort to make modding easy. As a result there are many mods for this game anywhere from AI vehicles (which really, I do think should be in the game eventually stock), to new Items, to different tech tree changes and more. Really everything about this game can be modded quickly and with ease. With a simple click for install and click for uninstall on the in game mod portal there will be no downloading sketchy mod loaders or fiddling about with  various hard to parse installation instructions.
As noted though, this is a game in early access and it is not complete. Bugs exist though they certainly arent game breaking and you wont find yourself with any saves broken by them. There are also a lot of planned features to the game (like nuclear energy for example), that arent yet in the stable version. This game has quite a ways to go, but in its current form, I do not think if you have seen some gameplay and like the looks of it, it will be a game you regret purchasing, unless of course you value your time (which this game will take in spades).

This is a game for those that like Infinifactory, maybe Space Engineers and more peaceful strategy games. This game has a good difficulty level that advances over time and I've played more than 30 hours, I still haven't completed the main campaign. I've been following this game since early development before the rocket parts were added to the game.
The late game is also nicely difficult and you are allowed to build very complex factories for your automation. The research tree is well balanced and the enemies evolve in the same time you evolve.
The only thing I don't like is that the red, green, blue research bottles are not realistic and makes no sense. Perhaps if it was explained what the bottle contains and how it works it would make sense but that's left to imagination. And there's no way to complete the game without having enemies in it, since you need the purple bottles. Playing this game on peaceful is fun enough for me so I have to use mods that allow purple bottles without the purple artefacts.
The performance is also superb. I'd like the developer of this game to develop another factory game set in a more peaceful environment, even with the screen full of moving parts on conveyors and robot machines everywhere, it still has a solid 60 fps even if you use the speedmult cheat.
The map generator is a solid working piece of equipment and has balanced seed for resources. You can tweak it before you start a custom scenario too.
In the late stage of the game you can also program the components using logic and logic gates. This allowed for more advanced systems of production where things can be produced on demand instead of forced on long conveyors.
It's worth 20 bucks, that's for sure.

Literal crack. Obviously a joke, but this game is incredibly addictive. I have over 600 hours in this game and all of it is legitimate. I don't idle this game. This game is a steal at $20, even in its current state, which I honestly don't feel it should be "early access."
It's a sandbox world where you get plopped on an alien world with just a miner and a furnace and you have to progress research and build efficient factories to launch a rocket. But, with the latest 0.15 update, that's not even really the end anymore. Launching a rocket brings back more science to progress the infinite research. It's megabase time!
I *do not suggest* this game to anyone who has problems with time management and commitments they need to keep. You will get lost in this game.
As long as you can manage your time properly, you should be able to handle this addiction, and I strongly suggest it to anyone with a technical mind. The whole game you are creating factories and try to be efficient as possible. There's no wrong ways to do anything, but there certainly is a most efficient way to do things... and you need to figure it out.
Don't forget: there will ALWAYS be a bottleneck.

Transistor is a good game, and it is worth playing. I beat it in around ~5 hours.
It is truly beautiful, both for the ears, and for the eyes. It really sucks you into a fantastic looking world, that leaves you silently thinking back on it once you've finished it. Artistically, the game is amazing.
However, the combat is just average. It's interesting, and kind of unique, mixing real time combat with some turn based element (being able to freeze everything to plan a move), but it gets repetitive, as the enemies don't feel that varied, and you end up mostly running in circles while your action bar is recharging. Also, you often have to wait a few seconds extra after each fight is done just so one of your skills comes off cool down, so that you can grab the monster EXP that's shield protected. If there were more fights like the final boss, it would feel more rewarding to play it.
The story is vaguely interesting, and unique - but not thrilling.
I feel that if the combat and story were just a bit better, the game would be a masterpiece, instead of simply being a good game.
Still, Transistor is a unique experience that is worth living :steamhappy:

Possible the best Star Wars game to date.
The story is 100% set in the Original Trilogy, constituting a credible prequel to Episode IV. It's completely devoid of any of the low quality fantasy stuff that has been forced down our throat such as Darth Kreya on a quest to "destroy the force" (I'm thiking of you, Chris Avellone) or Jerrod looking for the "valley of the Jedi" (your turn now, Justin Chin). In the front, we've got a war plot AS IN the Original Trilogy, with a war in the main stage and Jedi mysticism elegantly laying in the background,
The acting's pretty decent (Sam Witwer is great), cut scenes are nothing short of awesome, and the two or three throwbacks to the Prequel Trilogy (the "hologram" of Darth Maul, Bail Organa, the Jedi Temple made of Junk, and the Jedi Purge) are well executed. Two of the three DLCs (Tatooine and Hoth) provide an wesome icing to the cake, being a REAL pleasure to go through --the are "what-if"s in nature,with the evil ending protagonist taking a Vader-like role, rewriting parts of the Original Trilogy story in a damn well-connected manner. I only wish the ending to Hoth were a bit different.

Fans of oldschool dungeon crawler games will most probably love Legend of Grimrock, as it is an extremely well done dungeon crawler game.
While the game only has 3 classes, the different choices in skills make it possible to have multiple builds for each class - thus, there are multiple choices for how to build each of your 4 characters.
Combat is specially good in this game because, although the party can stand still and fight one monster, movement can be used to an advantage and, sometimes, it must be used, which adds to the level of challenge of the game. Managing items - weight, ammount and which items are or will be useful or not - is also a challenge by itself.
Multiple secrets in each level - and also in the game itself - add a LOT to the game.
The game, however, lacks in variety, both in items and enemies. There's little variation between equipment beyond their base values, with a few exceptions of weapons with special effects, and enemies repeat a lot throughout the levels.
Leveling up is also somewhat limited - I had the impression that I could get to the end of the game having one character max one skill while also keeping one or two other skills at somewhat decent levels, but I couldn't. And, many times, focusing entirely in one skill is not as good as it seems.
The biggest issue I had with the game was the last fight, mostly because it seemed badly designed to me. It's hard to explain without spoiling the fight, but I think people who have finished the game might understand why.
Despite its downsides, it's still an amazing game - and the level editor also adds a lot to the game, with some really interesting potential from the player-created levels I've seen.

I enjoy this game, unlike a lot of people I have no issues with performance and the AI skirmish battles are pretty fun. The skirmishes are ste up differently than Wargame with a defined front line and morale boosts or consequences from either being surrounded or in friendly territory. The skirmish is set into 3 stages whish I like and find more realistic. The stages are A. Recon- In this stage you are limited toalmost no tanks very little air support, and limited arty, however you get a lot of recon and a marginal amount of infantry units with fairly good anti tank to set up strategically. B. skirmish-This stage gives you access to higher ranks of A units and gives you the bulk of your fighting force with tanks bombers arty more reinforcements etc, In this stage you can start using a more dynamic front and start moving your units up and C. Battle? I think- This stage is more of a last minute reinforcement stage as I see it, perhaps if you are running low on reinforcements or you want better stats units, This stage will assist remaining units from stage B to really drive the Nazis back into the Vaterland or push the Allies back across the channel. They can also help a lot in defensive statures by helping spot and remaining calm under fire if you are not doing to well on the offensive

A really game changing feature that I love is getting all of your deployment points at the beginning of a phase, so you really have to be shrewd about the units you deploy, their location, and when you deploy them.

Overall, Steel Division is a very good game with lots of potential with DLC, and listening to the Player Community.
Pros:
While the organization and use of certain vehicles, and division compositions, can be picked apart for historical accuracy, the game overall stays very true to the 1944 period. The AI is extremely competitive and refined beyond any AI that could be encountered in outside RTS games such as Men of War, any game from the Total War Series, or even Theatre of War. Having not played Wargame, or any other Eugen RTS other then Ruse, I found the AI to be difficult but not impossible. When playing as the Germans who historically had limited manpower in real life (conscripts, ersatz forces, volksgrenadiers, and limted volksturm/hitlerjugend not included) along with limited materiel as in real life (The 17th SS which is a playable force in this game accurately only has Stug III and IV assault guns which was due to shortages of everything else in real life), this was especially true compared to my American counterparts who could send 15 Shermans and still have reserves. Lastly the battle deck system allows for a large amount of customization especially if you get with your friends to make specialized decks for teamplay between you two, (An infantry division's static defenses and fodded combined with the hard punch of a panzer division or mechanized division makes a deadly combo.) Overall Steel Division is off to a great start as a game.
Cons:
There is some historical accuracy sacrificed for balancing but this is necessary and completely understandable, but hardcore WWII buffs, you have been warned.
Campaign: The Campaign is very action packed which can be good in some RTS settings however going from Skirmishes which have mixed engagements and the occassional full offensive, or the tutorial which is very small in battle scale to a massive battle involving 40+ units on the map at any given point and vast overwhelming force with a historic background but no story can be underwhelming for those who prefer a story-based campaign. Hopefully in the future, DLCs will be added that add small scale missions, (a pathfinder mission of small scale to lead Airborne Troops to victory by securing behind the line areas would be amazing, or a small scale Michael Wittman mission at Villers Bocage etc).
Hopes for this Game in the near and far future:
More Divisions- Such as the 1st and 2nd SS which were very infamous fighting forces in and around Normandy, and considering a Swastika is already used certain versions of Steel Division (mine included) for the flag of the German Forces, as long as the frontline fighting was kept in the foremost consideration, then this would not be unreasonable.
More Models- It would be interesting to see more camo patterns applied to the infantry and various vehicles throughout the war.
More Missions- Small scale fights, scenarios, or situations that can be entertaining, engaging, or perhaps intuitive for future skirmishes and multiplayer matches.
More Fronts: DLCs that could add earlier and later fronts in the game such as France in 1940, or perhaps Poland in 1939, all the way to the final days of Germany in 1945 on the Western Front.
More Factions: On the same tangent as fronts, perhaps add more nations fighting in the war in Europe, obviously the Soviets come to mind (T34 spam would be unreal) along with the Italians and perhaps a division each dedicated to Romania, Hungary, Bulgaria, etc. This would allow for interesting units, gameplay dynamics, and allow the newbie player to be better immersed and at least informed in the smaller areas of the war.
Overall I highly reccomend this game even without all the hopes that were just listed, as the base game on its own is amazing and allows for much more content that could come in the form of DLCs or perhaps the start of a new game franchise or even as a collection of mods in the Workshop!

This one's a little tough, because I really wanted to like this game. I'm a fan of survival games and sims (both with and without capital-S). Spacebase DF9 has a nice idea and a rather decent realisation. The gameplay is all right, and the design, particularly of the inhabitants of the space station, is pretty cool. BUT. The game has been abandoned by the devs and currently relies on community patches to work. Don't expect any fixes for the bugs that are still in the game.
What is there is the groundwork for the Sims in space. Sort of. You're starting out with three astronauts and a small amount of resources, just enough to build a closed space to shelter your little aliens from, well, actual space. From there, you mine resources, add to your space station room by room, and slowly develop a complex microcosmos that has you manage life-sustaining installations like reactors and oxygen generators, necessities like food dispensers, a medical bay and bedrooms, and luxuries like a bar and a fitness room. Additional challenges include raids and abandoned drifting space stations to discover and loot to your heart's content.
But that's where the content ends. It's a very bare-bones game that gets repetitive fast. The AI is borderline stupid as soon as something goes wrong, with people running around screaming at the tiniest fire instead of using the extinguishers and subsequently letting the entire station burn, others starving to death because the food dispenser was too far away (in the next room), and the doctor preferring to eat five times in a row at said food dispenser instead of incinerating the bodies of those who died in the last pirate raid - who have only died because security idled at the opposite end of the station until I specifically directed them to fight the raiders. You have to micromanage everything, because you can't trust the AI. Even after you assign jobs to people, they will sometimes refuse to do them, even if it's their preferred occupation. Security officers will not intervene unless you tell them to, and then one at a time, getting killed by absurdly overpowered raiders.
Who will always show up as soon as your station hits a certain number of people (ridiculously low, six, if I remember right), and will start out super-strong. Contrary to what the "map" selection suggests, there is no way to adjust the difficulty unless you change the game files manually, and even then it often doesn't work. The area of space that you pick has no tangible impact on how hard the game is; the number of raiders and meteor strikes seems consistent across the board, the only thing that changes is how often empty stations drift by yours.
It's crazy hard to survive after hitting the threshold after which raiders spawn, and borderline impossible once you've reached ten and higher because the game keeps spawning higher and higher numbers of enemies, forcing you to assign around half of your inhabitants to security. That, in turn, prevents you from playing a lot of the other features, like botany, which you need for the bar, or science, which you need for almost all upgrades. The balance is shoddy, and Double Fine did not bother to fix it, instead abandoning the game.
Fans have stepped in and created one (to my knowledge, so far) patch to fix a few of these bugs, but there is no guarantee it'll work with your game. And it shouldn't have to, if DF didn't stop working on games once it becomes too much work. It seems like the game didn't sell as many copies as they anticipated, and they decided it wasn't worth the effort, instead starting another crowdfunding campaign for a new game. That looks like a really shady business practice, like you'd find on the seedier side of Greenlight and Early Access, and one I can't support.
Shame. This would have been a fun space sim, but as it is, I can't recommend it.

Being a fan of the old “Tycoon” games and “Theme Hospital” I was really excited about Space Base DF-9. I thought for sure reviewers were being too hard on it, so as soon as I saw it pop up in a Humble Bundle I was ecstatic… But, all of my excitement was for naught. Almost 6 hours wasted and I can pretty well guarantee I will never touch this title again.
There is a ton of promise here. When the game is running smooth there’s not a lot to complain about (except maybe lack of construction options), but eventually that smooth ride will be over and you’ll realize nothing works like it should, if at all. So while playable you’ll hit a point where the effort to advance isn’t worth it. If you still think you want to punish yourself by playing this game make sure you check out
for the unofficial patch, the mechanics are still broken but everything else has been improved.
The basic construction and management section of the game is fairly well done. It’s very similar to “Theme Hospital”, but with a slightly improved interface. That’s where the positives end. So many things are broken that it becomes unnecessarily difficult, and not in a fun, challenging way but in a “oh there’s another thing that doesn’t work right” kind of way.
Here are just a few examples of things you’ll see characters do:
- Die of suffocation despite being surrounded by rooms with oxygen and having access to an airlock with space suits,
- Become incapacitated (not dead, just lying around uselessly) indefinitely. If they’re Raiders they actually might be back up and start killing people!
- Be marked for the brig or infirmary but never go there
- Scientists not researching (despite being assigned research and having a research station).
- Ignore the 3 fire extinguishers near the fire, and instead stomp on it until they catch on fire, then run around the base being ignored by everyone else until they burn to death… Actually that might’ve been the most entertaining part of the game!

The user interface is easy to navigate but overly simple. You only have 1 save slot and the game auto saves by default, so if you’re not careful it’s quite easy to erase a save game by clicking on the wrong thing and not exiting before it overwrites your game.
The graphics are fine. They’re quite obviously a throwback to “Theme Hospital” (how many times can I name dop?). It works well for the genre, and they’re fairly sharp.
The sound is outright boring, the music is nothing impressive and off the top of my head I honestly don’t remember any sounds other than that and the chirping alarm if you zoom in far enough.
This game could be so good, but as in so many cases now it looks like the developer took their money and ran. In my love/hate relationship with Early Access this is why the hate portion exists. I’d give it a 3/10, it’s playable and as long as things work right it’s quite enjoyable, but the unpredictable and frustrating broken mechanics make it another EA Trash title. Pick it up in a bundle with some good games or for $1 or less and get a couple hours of fun… But DO NOT, under any circumstances pay any more for it than that. Especially when you could get the vastly superior Theme Hospital and forget this all together.

For disclaimer: This game is amazing, well every version but the german one anyways because I've been told by friends and also reading other negative reviews that the german version censors much of the gameplay, but I digress. This game is great, I've played it a ton on console in the past, it controls great, gameplay is fluid, story is alright, not really anything to write home about, music is iffy, some licensed stuff and a few bands I kinda like quite a bit like The Parlor Mob, Kasabian and Trivium to name a few, but mostly it comprises of either really underground or strictly in-house music groups I couldn't find info on, which is kinda lame. Not a perfect game, but it's solid to say the least. Think True Crime but good and developed by a company that knows how to make good video games.
So if the game is great, why the negative review? Well, the Steam release seems to be rather buggy and prone to crashing. Literally after every mission, the game would crash on me. I don't know if Sleeping Dogs just doesn't run well with AMD hardware, but even on the lowest settings, it would still crash regularly after a single mission was completed. I'm not the only one that experienced this problem either, some people couldn't even get the game to run, so it seems to be a consistent problem for some folks. And my computer can run the Saints Row games and Overwatch on high settings and stream it and not have any problems with crashing, so I know it's not my rig being not powerful enough to run the game properly.
I seriously hope this issue gets resolved. I thought maybe it was just the definitive version causing the crashes and looked into getting the standard copy of Sleeping Dogs without the DLC, but of course that was taken off the store (thanks Steam!), so I suppose I will never know. I bought the game when it was on sale for $5 and immediately got my refund for it after the 4th time it crashed, so no real loss. In conclusion, the game is great. If you can get it to run properly on PC, great, but if not, that's a shame. Buy it for console, this is just one example of PC not always being superior to console, and I say that as a PC gamer. Recommended, just not on Steam!

The most important thing to understand about this game is that it absolutely is not ... not ... an old-school RPG.  If you are looking for an old-school RPG this is not what you're looking for.  I would go so far as to say the suggestion that it is an old-school RPG is borderline false advertising.
This is a puzzle game wrapped in the trappings of an old-school RPG, and played in real time rather than turn-based.  Combat is a dance puzzle with button mashing.  There are no tactics.  Magic is encumbered with rune selection, which must be done in real time, making casters a liability.  Rogues are just another combatant, there is no thieving.
There is no story to speak of.  When you're not solving puzzles, you are seeking hidden buttons and pattern differences in wall tiles.
Is it fun?  Yes, it's not bad as far as puzzle games go, nor is it anything special.  Yet, it's nothing but a puzzle game and that wasn't what I wanted.  I usually avoid Indie games, and now I will never buy an Indie game again.  I feel like I was conned, and robbed, and that this game has been intentionally marketed to fool old-school gamers for profit.

One of the poorest quality PC ports available on Steam.
Control and video options have to be set in a launcher outside the game, and the options available in-game are barebones, not even including an option for subtitles in-game, let alone cutscenes.
Combat is unnecessarily difficult. The lock-on key is useless, and force powers are extremely difficult to aim. Lifted enemies and objects fly in crazy directions that don't seem to take any input from keys pressed or mouse movements. Boss battles add to the frustration, as bosses can shrug off force powers and lightsaber attacks with impunity, and often seem to be completely invincible during scripted movement and combat sequences.
Even on my relatively nice gaming rig (GTX 680 x2, i7 3820 @3.6Ghz, 32Gbs RAM) this game suffers constant stuttering, and  odd split-second flashes of other scenes when using some force powers and lightsaber attacks.
Just from a technical standpoint this game is a failure, but the ridiculous (and unfortunately canon) storyline only pushes this pile of garbage further into the "forgetful" realm of gaming. It's hard to choke down even as an avid Star Wars fan.
-5/10

Ok, so after a few days of playing this game I think that it's time to write a review.
I like this game a lot, but it's not perfect. Here are the pros and cons:
-Pretty good 2D visuals.
-An extensive roster of characters(36 characters in total)
-Improved netcode compared to the console version.
-Unlike the console version, the DLC characters are free and are aviable from the start.
-You can edit the colors of every character
-Can be played very well using the keyboard(well, at least 80% of the characters)
-There is a tutorial to teach you the basics of this game(the types of jumps, drive cancels, max cancels, etc)
-Matchmaking is very inconsitant during ranked matches(well I think that this is at least for me.....)
-The net code is input delay based, wich means that the game will run at the average speed but there is going to be a delay between your inputs and the actions of your character(only if you have problems with your internet).
-Online mode dosen't have Spectator mode, so if you are waiting for a match you either watch the menu, or do something else on the internet.
-Replays are buggy, sometimes when you watch one, the characters will stand still in the middle of the match until the time runs out.
I will recomend this game to those that are into fighting games
I strongly encourage any fighting game fan to give this game a try or even better. Just purchase it!

This game is in Early access. Thats normally a turn off for me, and I buy games based on what Im getting at the time I buy it as opposed to promises, but in this game, as it stands right now, this game easily has enough content to justify its 25 CAD/20 USD price tag (which apparently will never change or go on sale according to the devs).
This game is about optimization and micromanagement. If you dont like that, you wont like it. There isnt really any sort of visual element to building your bases/factories etc as pretty much all items are functional and affect the gameplay. There is a lot of tedious busy work even after setting up a nicely running factory, but thats kind of what you sign up for with a game like this. With tons of tech tree unlocks to research, then eventually farm materials for and manufacture, this is not a game youll be done with quickly and has quite a lot of content.
Campaign wise, so far, there is one major campaign which has a somewhat interesting story I suppose, but really focuses on teaching you the basics all the way through the campaign. Its not that its drawn out and unnecessary (Though it could be a  little shorter), but that this game has so many different Items, short cuts, systems to work with that to be competent, I think its a good idea to play through the campaign first.
That might seem weird, as if Im saying the campaign isnt where youll be spending most of your time, and thats because that is indeed the case. While the campaign is ok, and from a purely dollars to time point of view thats all fine and dandy, the core of this game is the freeplay mode where you can build out, try different scenarios from different seeds with different settings, with people, without people many different ways. Each one of these games lasts quite some time too. Much like minecraft, do not ever expect to be done with that world within an hour. It no typical mission and you can expect a game to last days of in game time.
Why does it last so long? the micro management. It really does start off slow, but when you start building off your factory things speed up somewhat. I personally feel that the pacing is a bit slow making you feel like youre doing more busy work than necessary especially at the start, but it does not kill the game. Unfortunately though, it does mean that often times, when you want to leave it sitting and running in the background, things can go awry quickly. Now, a lot of this is avoidable, probably simply by being better than I am, but I doubt you can completely escape this. The good news though is that even if thats not ideal for you, this game has great mod support, so you can change it to your liking.
Mod support is great. Though not on the steam workshop and through its own mod portal, modding is made easy with  an outlined frame work and drag and drop installations. On the modders side of things, it seems they put in the effort to make modding easy. As a result there are many mods for this game anywhere from AI vehicles (which really, I do think should be in the game eventually stock), to new Items, to different tech tree changes and more. Really everything about this game can be modded quickly and with ease. With a simple click for install and click for uninstall on the in game mod portal there will be no downloading sketchy mod loaders or fiddling about with  various hard to parse installation instructions.
As noted though, this is a game in early access and it is not complete. Bugs exist though they certainly arent game breaking and you wont find yourself with any saves broken by them. There are also a lot of planned features to the game (like nuclear energy for example), that arent yet in the stable version. This game has quite a ways to go, but in its current form, I do not think if you have seen some gameplay and like the looks of it, it will be a game you regret purchasing, unless of course you value your time (which this game will take in spades).

This is a game for those that like Infinifactory, maybe Space Engineers and more peaceful strategy games. This game has a good difficulty level that advances over time and I've played more than 30 hours, I still haven't completed the main campaign. I've been following this game since early development before the rocket parts were added to the game.
The late game is also nicely difficult and you are allowed to build very complex factories for your automation. The research tree is well balanced and the enemies evolve in the same time you evolve.
The only thing I don't like is that the red, green, blue research bottles are not realistic and makes no sense. Perhaps if it was explained what the bottle contains and how it works it would make sense but that's left to imagination. And there's no way to complete the game without having enemies in it, since you need the purple bottles. Playing this game on peaceful is fun enough for me so I have to use mods that allow purple bottles without the purple artefacts.
The performance is also superb. I'd like the developer of this game to develop another factory game set in a more peaceful environment, even with the screen full of moving parts on conveyors and robot machines everywhere, it still has a solid 60 fps even if you use the speedmult cheat.
The map generator is a solid working piece of equipment and has balanced seed for resources. You can tweak it before you start a custom scenario too.
In the late stage of the game you can also program the components using logic and logic gates. This allowed for more advanced systems of production where things can be produced on demand instead of forced on long conveyors.
It's worth 20 bucks, that's for sure.

Literal crack. Obviously a joke, but this game is incredibly addictive. I have over 600 hours in this game and all of it is legitimate. I don't idle this game. This game is a steal at $20, even in its current state, which I honestly don't feel it should be "early access."
It's a sandbox world where you get plopped on an alien world with just a miner and a furnace and you have to progress research and build efficient factories to launch a rocket. But, with the latest 0.15 update, that's not even really the end anymore. Launching a rocket brings back more science to progress the infinite research. It's megabase time!
I *do not suggest* this game to anyone who has problems with time management and commitments they need to keep. You will get lost in this game.
As long as you can manage your time properly, you should be able to handle this addiction, and I strongly suggest it to anyone with a technical mind. The whole game you are creating factories and try to be efficient as possible. There's no wrong ways to do anything, but there certainly is a most efficient way to do things... and you need to figure it out.
Don't forget: there will ALWAYS be a bottleneck.

TL;DR: Gameplay Good; Cohesive feeling world/storytelling Bad.
Transistor's gameplay is interesting and unique. The playstyle can change on the fly, either due to loosing a function, or because you've chosen to try a new combination of functions. It's like a mini-chess battle each encounter, strategizing your moves and placement relative to how you know the other pieces (enemies) will respond and move. I have played through the entire game, and I am planning to play the Recursion() (basically New Game+).
I will say however, I did *not* find the story telling to be good. I see a lot of positive reviews on the story, but to me it's actually somewhat obnoxious and pretentious. I will give Supergiant credit because the way the story is told is unique, but I always think the story is bad. There isn't a lot of reasons for how the world is the way it is and why it would work that way. They are taking a lot on suspension of disbelief, which I can do for most games, but for this game, it felt like two different worlds: the gameplay world (awesome futuristic tech) and the story world (emotional, and a heaping dose of cliche revenge, with a♥♥♥♥♥♥Tracy vibe). It just didn't quite mesh well for me. But, the gameplay is really fun and interesting. It almost feels like the gameplay and story were developed in separate rooms and then pasted together.

Transistor is probably one of the best games i've played in a while, and i was actually going through the second playthrough slower because i didn't want it to end. The soundtrack is amazing and fits with the story very well. The gameplay is super fun and i was actually surprised at how many combinations you could do so no it won't get repetitive at all. If your hesistant, give it a try, you won't be dissapointed.

The original Rollercoaster Tycoon is not only one of the most favourite games from my childhood, but it is one of my favourite and most loved games of all time.
Rollercoaster Tycoon still holds up until this day.  The mechanics may seem a little clunky compared to back in 1999, but that should not pushh you away from buying this game.
In Rollercoaster Tycoon you need to build a theme park to complete a set of objectives set out for you at the beginning of each scenario. Some of these objectives can be completed easily while others will take quite a bit of time.  There is many different theme parks and scenarios to chose from, as this version of Rollercoaster Tycoon also includes the expansions!  Pretty good for £4.79.
There are many different attractions to unlock from Merry Go Round's to Viking Ship to huge Rollercoasters; which is done through researching.  The researching mechanic is really straightforward,  the player needs to select from a bunch of preset options from "minimum" to "maximum"  each option has a different cost attached to it.
The game is not called Rollercoaster Tycoon for no reason!  The game enables the player to design and create their own custom rollercoaster from scratch!  Make every turn and drop of the track completely unique.  Watch that excitement rating! Players can also create rides such as log flumes, kart racing and even transport attractions such as a monorail.
Of course, you need staff to run a theme park.  The player can recruit four different types of staff:  Handyman, Mechanic, Security and Entertainer.  The handyman is used to keep the staff tidy, water plants and mow the lawn,  the mechanic of course repairs any broken down rides while the security keeps those annoyances away meanwhile the entertainer is busy...well, entertaining people in many different cute and quirky costumes.
The game offers quite a few customization options.  The player can set how fast a ride can go - Watch out, don't let it crash and kill your guests! Decorations such as statues, water features, plants and trees are available.  Fences, benches and trash cans are needed to keep guests happy!
If you have fond memories of this game and are reading reviews to make sure it isn't just nostalgia making you interested in the purchase - I found say go for it.  This game is still solid and truly holds up.  Meanwhile, if you have not played this game and are looking for something fun and relaxing, yet potentially challenging; I would say that you owe it to yourself to play this classic game.
Please note:  The steam overlay does not work in this game.  Meaning you can not press shift + tab to look at friends, guides, achievements, etc, because of this Rollercoaster Tycoon does not support screenshots.  The resolution is off too - This game can not be played on full screen on my monitor.
Now, go charge your guests a $100 entrance fee and overcharge on all food, drinks and rides!
EDIT: This is a fantastic game that should win the "The Test of Time" award in the Steam Game Awards 2016!

I was pleasantly surprised by Assault Android Cactus. I usually am not a huge fan of the twin stick shooter genre because frankly I am usually not very good at them. The main reason I am terrible at these games is that I have a hard time avoiding enemies when there is a bunch of things happening on the screen at one time.
Therefore I really liked the idea behind the battery power. In Assault Android Cactus you don't die when your lose all of your health. Instead you are stunned. You need to make sure that your android doesn't run out of battery power though. In order to recharge your batteries you need to kill enough enemies in order to have one drop a battery powerup. I liked that Assault Android Cactus allowed you to focus on killing enemies instead of spending all your time trying to avoid enemy projectiles.
The only major issues I had with the game was the length and difficulty. The main storyline only takes four to five hours to complete. Outside of the bosses the game is quite easy and you will rarely die.
If you hate twin stick shooters you won't like Assault Android Cactus. If you have even a passing interest in the genre I would recommend picking up the game at some point either at full retail or during a sale.
Note: I received a free review copy of the game from the developer.

I like to leave legitimate reviews for games, despite how "serious" the game is.  So this review will be no different.
If you remember AIM (AOL Instant Messenger), then you will feel the nostalgia bomb the minute you start the game for the first time.  That's mostly the reason why I got this, aside from the obvious laugh (and easy 100% achievement).
The plot is basically that you are a dude in his senior year of high school, and he clearly likes this girl named Emily, which he talks to regularly on AIM.
The interaction itself is Emily writing a message to you on AIM, and then you choosing 1,2 or 3 on your keyboard, which correlate to different responses.  The chapters are based on years, so while you start in your senior year of high school, you progress until your senior year of college before the game ends.
The "game story" itself is linear.  You can get different responses based on the choices you make, but at the end of college, the result is always the same.  And it's quite a sad ending, to be honest.
The game is free to play, so obviously you really don't need to be reading reviews.  It's an enjoyable experience mixed in with some nostalgia and some other feels.  I recommend it based on all of the things mentioned in this review.
Kudos to the game creator, Kyle Seeley, for taking the time and effort to put together a nifty little point and click experience for all of us that came from that era of the Internet.
I, for one, will always remember the many years I spent on AIM.  Growing up, posting lyrics away messages and adding quotes to my profile so I could look cool to everybody else.
Download this game and enjoy the feels of 2002 all over again.
----
As for the achievements: once you complete the game, you can go back and start the first "Chapter" again.  Enter "Password123" as your screen name and then anything as your name.  It will unlock all of the icons you need to use to get all of the achievements.
From there, just select the icon, engage in brief conversation with Emily until she acknowledges your icon.  At that point, the achievement will be unlocked.
Repeat the first year again and again with the same screen name as I mentioned to get all of the achievements.

KOF games story and functionality wise have often gone in waves. Every game brings a bit of a change up to the table, but collectively there's legs of the journey. One that's often come with an interesting story that waves just a bit sharper than most fighting game tittles of such background. Capcom still can't keep a major story of how Chun Li's father died. And to think SNK use to make this KOF collection of fighters from several of their games once every year.
With the Orochi Saga leg, Nests Saga, and whatever you might call the last stretch of games through KOF 11 where they stoped giving them numbers on years and just sequal numbers, I'm not sure if we're in a SAGA, or just progressing a story that through the tournament that Rugal's children now sponsor, seemingly not being evil, another faction that seems very evil is using it toward their ends in plots that could undo Mankind as we know it. And like Jedah from the ye old DarkStalkers franchise, they seem to be a kind of re occuring evil that can go back and try again until something in a timeline changes.
And the way they do this when all is said in done is smart as they find the best way to deal with a character many don't like that let's them finally leave the franchise, and yet also earns the character perhaps a bit more respect. Leave it to SNK to actually make a story that does some justice, and delivers a damn fine engine worthy of the tradition. It's not without a few flaws, but some of the likes come with tittles that look to recreate what they've been doing a bit.
The Cons:
The move lists are not to the hgiher counts like later in the Saga legs tittles like 98 or 2003 tended to bring, but much of the core moves known to characters are there and many with slight changes on their approaches to how they function.
@#$$ I still miss Terry Bogard's "Power Dunk" move. I really #$%^ing do.
The Music is decent, but not sure I'd call it the great music styles that SNK got into back in it's earlier years that made you feel the character and situation all the further. It just lacks some of that catchy factor, but it's fitting.
If you're new to the franchise, it tells a story you can hop on right now and find some interest, but the real treat is in for people who do a little back searching into the rich story universe of SNK and how it's connected. Trust me the SNK universe is worth it, which is kind of a PRO if you're willing to do a little research.
BAD AND GOOD.
And finally I'm not sure I dig how the super bar is basically turned into two seperate bars. One is stockable and needed for your super specials, but to pull a NeoMax move, you need the top bar full too, or use that top power bar above the oragne to go into a powered up mode to so the neomax. But if you do you can in theory peform not only a special into a super special, but a Super Special into your NeoMax move. The things you can pull become a massive game changer.
When you pull some heavy hititng stuff in SNK, you know it, and you feel it. Sometimes on the recieving end you feel it a bit much, but otherwise it feels rewarding and creats it's sense of danger. But the multi bars turn it into feeling a bit more cumbersom in requirements than at first most may like.
THE VERY GOODS
Mai is back. Anyone who follows SNK will know what I'm talking about. No Mai no buy as they say.
The flash and flare is there and feels like it bellongs but makes for some good wow moments. In fact the all over 2D fighter package looks good and yet not disorienting.
Controls are good, yet not over the top forgiving. You get what you pull, and when you figure out what you're doing wrong and get it right, you're going to know it and do plenty better as a reward for doing it right, and it will stick with you if you play semi regularly.
Classic Yuri and King clothing malfunctions after special moves are back. Ask a veteran, or beat Yuri or King with a special move and up and you'll understand what I mean. Yes, it's necessairy.
Combos can be impressive, but you work for them, and chances are with the team three on three broken up matches they give you good oppertunity to turn things around, and the combos aren't super over the top to the level you should just put your controller down and die like Marvel vs Capcom 3.
Play Iori in both his forms without extra DLC cost.
A certain someone not only dies, they utterly get undone from the universe, and most of you will applaud how it's done.
The game simply looks as nice as it feels for someone to play, and you can get things done as a newer player or a veteran. With the way the team system works too, you really can pass the controller with a friend if you choose to team up and face the world online or the computer, or even local friends. Sometimes it dosn't need to be a tag match for it to be a good team endeavor.
Unlock colors by simply playing the game to customize the character palates for quite the different looks. Maybe even put yourself in the shoes of one of the many SNK characters you really relate too. There's characters for every kind of fighting fan, make a few your own.
WRAP UP
It's a solid game, plenty worth it's 20 dollar price tag these days, and if you'd really like to see how KOF has evolved, the tripple pack here on STEAM basically gives you the total up game play of some of the past high points of the KOF franchise. If you watch a play through of the other years to get some story, then play the wrap up leg tittle for yourself, like playing 98 witch has the best of everything non story wise from 94 to 97, or watch what happens up till the next year available on STEAM and then play that one, it can be a rather rewarding experience. Or hell, hunt down the other tittles and play them if you can. But seriously, at least peek out the story universe of the other tittles and play the leg wrap up tittles so you can feel the story as you come to understand it, even the once hidden characters that were a part of the story unfolding.
With the STEAM tripple pack, you get those wrap up milestones of the series in a good final form, each one a bit different. Who knows, it may inspire you to look back into the depths of SNK and how the connections run deep, and get a piece of the fighting tradition that now and again in ways rivaled Capcom, a company that was very thrilled and supportive of it's fans.
PS: Beware those who hold liniage with the Orochi blood. Baddie characters and characters with just cause alike. Beware the Blood Riot. All part of a story universe you'll learn to respect.

This is a unique mix between a Bejeweled style tile-matching game and a tower defense-ish game.
You have to match tiles within the limited amount of turns and/or time to summon your units. This is where things can start getting frustrating. Sometimes you have to choose between passing the level or hopefully matching enough coin tiles to allow you to upgrade your units.
It's just frustrating enough to make a microtransaction for in-game currency tempting.
Natural grinders can push through it, but anyone else may start having issues with it.
Despite the need to really grind or fork out cash for enough gold to upgrade your units, I find this game enjoyable and would recommend it to those looking for a weird twist on a favorite genre.

Paper Please... Or should we say, "Border Simulator" !
As the name suggests it, you will be an immigration officer/inspector entitled to filter people coming at the border of the most beautiful and democratic country in the (fictive) world: Arstotzka ! Accepting people or denying their entrance on the territory through a harsh and meticulous control... Or have mercy and pity for some of them despite their false documents, just to potentially see the fall of this dictatorship in which you are living.
Simple graphics, quite common for an indie... But the true and particular interesting point of the game is all about these cornelian dillema you will encounter... Will you accept the bribe you will get offered by immigrants to let them through ? (Knowing that your family is sick)... Or will you stay faithful to your country and fulfill your duty as the party told you ?... Hard choice yes, and each one of them could lead you to a different ending.
The gameplay is also quite simple: Controlling, controlling, controlling... However, you will quickly see that the more documents required to check... The more time you will spend at controlling... And the less money you will get... And no, do not even imagine that you get tons of money for th job. As you see, you will have to choose.
In synthesis:
A really pleasant indie game to have in your library. Of course, i would advise to play it just for few minutes per day as its gameplay style is obviously repeitive... But still, if you have ever dreamed to work as immigration officer within a communis country... Just go for it an you will be nicely surprised ! :)

“Better than GTA in every Wei”
Kung Fu films have their classics. “The 36th Chamber of Shaolin”, “Last Hurrah for Chivalry” and “Heroes of the East” are a few movies that spring to mind. For Kung Fu video games I’d pick “Double Dragon II”, “River City Ransom” and “Sleeping Dogs”.
The Definitive Edition has all the DLC from the original title. Including the two stand alone story missions. The graphics and PC performance has also been improved.
The problem with games like Grand Theft Auto is that the playable characters are all career criminals. With no chance of redemption. I cannot even hope to empathize with the likes of “crazy” Trevor or “corrupted family guy” Michael from GTA5. Sleeping Dogs is different. You play as undercover cop Wei Shen. He's a good guy caught up in a bad situation. I can understand his struggle and appreciate his point of view.
I love Skyrim. I’ve poured over 100 hours into the game on my PS3 (don’t laugh). But still the melee combat leaves a lot to be desired. It can be a little clunky at the best of times. In comparison the combat in Sleeping Dogs is near flawless. Wei can track his targets and counter attack with ease. Even when you’re fighting ten guys in the pouring rain the combat remains fluid and fun. Using a gamepad to play is strongly recommended if you want to have the best experience.
The City of Hong Kong is a vibrant place with it’s neon lights, market stalls and Karaoke bars (Wei’s actually a pretty good singer!). Performance wise the Definitive Edition runs at a rock solid 60fps at 1080p. There are also some excellent FAQ's in the Steam community if you get stuck on something.
Criminally overshadowed by the GTA series. Sleeping Dogs is better in every Wei.

The Transitor is an action role-playing game set in the fictional city of Cloudbank. Playing as the city's famous singer, Red who loses her voice to a shadowy band of elites called the Camerata, it is immediately clear from the outset that this is a very stylish game. From the neon-lit environments that you explore, to the harmonic, electronic synth music that flows out, players are in for an audio-visual treat that gives the game a distinctive look, feel and style.
To describe The Transistor as a beautiful game however is like describing Monet as being handy with a brush. Made by Supergiant Games of Bastion fame, it is no surprise to see such ability and confidence in the art direction. Allied to this is a robust and diverse combat system that provides players with many approaches for which they can do battle. A balanced system it is too as it gives both tactical depth and reward for carving out your own distinctive playstyle. Key to this is the opportunity for the player to freeze time and map out their moves strategically mid-battle.
Nonetheless, whilst the combat is satifying, more use could have been made of puzzle elements within the game to change the pace and offer greater variety. In particular, there was a segment at the start where the player had to utilise Red's ability to freeze time to open a door. Such instances hinted at a promise of more brain-teasing puzzles ahead, only for this promise to go unfulfilled.
There are also instances where the relatively fixed isometric viewpoint of Red's actions and movements can jar against the rigid environments. Several instances take place where you lose track of Red because she is hidden behind some structure or wall. That said, for the most part, these cases are few and far between.
Beyond the aesthetics and the solid gameplay systems lie an strong and original plot that perfectly compliments the two aforementioned features. Central to the story is the relationship between Red and the Transitor, a large heavy broadsword that houses the voice of a mysterious man. Whilst Red herself cannot speak, the silent void is filled by the voice in the Transitor, and through the subtle sways in her manner and some utterly delightful cutscenes, we begin to see something burgeoning. It speaks much about the game's writer, Greg Kasavin, that he is able to convey all this without much in the way of dialogue between the two protaganists. All of this fills the final ending scene with special resonance. Put simply, your author hasn't seen such a strong ending in a videogame for a long while.
By itself, the feel of The Transistor's storyline is enough to carry any game. When combined with a richly satisfying combat system, and an art-style that has flair in abundance, then these aspects dovetail together to cement The Transistor as a phenomenal game that lingers in your mind and your heart well after the ending credits roll.

A first-person dungeon crawler set in a series of underground labyrinths, filled with monsters, puzzles and traps.
Rating 7/10
A throwback to the early 90s role-playing games like Eye of the Beholder, Ultima Underworld and Stonekeep. Whilst in many ways Legend of Grimrock is a homage to those early games it's worth buying not just for nostalgia but because it's a great game in it's own right.
In updating the classic formula they haven't changed much, grid-based movement, advancing one tile at a time with 90 degree turns. The party consists of four different characters spread across three classes, the fighters in the front row and the more vulnerable mage and Rogue in the back row. The two in the front row will deal the most damage and take the most damage via melee combat, the two characters in the back row can use magic and ranged attacks. It's a fine balance and timing is key in order to keep your party alive.
Combat suffers from the same limitations as it did in the games Grimrock is trying to re-create, wait for the enemy to enter the tile in front of you before unleashing all of your attacks then back away or strafe sideways before they have a chance to return damage. Rinse and repeat. There are obviously times this strategy doesn't always work such as being surrounded by three or more enemies or backing into a dead end but it's the strategy you'll end up using the most. It worked back in the 90s and it still works now.
There is a story loosely attached but it's not really important, this is a dungeon crawler at heart and the fun comes from fighting your way through and solving puzzles in each new level of the dungeon. There are no quests to speak of other than to survive the dungeon. During the game you pick up clues and lore via letters left by a previous prisoner called Toorum, it's a simple but effective way of building up some atmosphere and history to the adventure.
It's a bit too easy and a bit too short. I completed the game twice unlocking all achievements, completing my second play through on Hard Boiled and Doin' It Old School and even then I completed it with little effort. Aside from making the game longer I felt it would have benefited from a few NPCs, something Stonekeep did to great effect. It would have broken up the game play a bit and offered something different. However these are fairly minor disappointments to what is otherwise a superb game.
Looking forward to Legend of Grimrock 2.

Prepare to die, again and again. 'Legend of Grimrock' is a hardcore RPG even in normal difficulty. Either I made all the wrong choices either your party is always at a (more than slight) disadvantage as you get to higher levels. I've been poisoned and eaten alive by spiders, incinerated by those flying armored mages, and even chewed up by frosty lizards. The devs really want you to suffer in this dungeon that often seems like a dead end as it's almost impossible to fight and defeat more than one enemy at the time. All the fighting is done real time but there are no shortcuts or hotkeys, therefore the computer will always be quicker then you as you will struggle to command the attack with your mouse - especially with the spells that need several inputs : choosing the wand, choosing 1-4 runes, and then pressing on the attack button AGAIN! But most of all the puzzles will drive you crazy: 'The Maze of Madness' will drive you as mad as hell until you can't take it anymore (or find the improbable solution with no hints whatsoever) and the mostly random logic will leave your characters and yourself starving while you bang your head against the wall.
The minimalistic nature of the game is classy, but the lack of real meaning to many of the puzzles is frustrating; some are genuinely good and easy to understand thanks to a scroll (the shadow maze for instance), but now I'm currently stuck in an endless hall in level 9. There's probably a hint I'm missing somewhere in the slaughterfest but maybe I'll die before I find it. I might never see the light of day, after all I've been there for over 24h already...Grimrock don't roll, it's a total headbanger!
PS: I eventually found the scroll and got to the game's over-the-top goofy conclusion; you have to see it to believe it! Also the level editor is great and relatively easy to use and some of the mods are actuallly way more enjoyable than the original, there's this awesome Mine of Malan Vael and The Tower of Bones that could both easily be official DLCs while we are all waiting for the sequel.

Theres a lot that can be said about this game but I'm going to keep this short and simple because frankly I think that the overwelming amount of positive reviews speaks for itself.
This game is one of those games where graphics mean virtually nothing. The whole point is to create an infectious disease or contagion that infects all of humanity and the kill them. It's absurdly simple sounding but it suprisingly takes a lot of skill in the higher difficulties. In fact this game rewards aggressive players, the only real restriction to playing this way though is balancing out lethality with infectivity since you need to infect faster than you kill.
The menu system pre-game is rather nice as it gives you options for pre-game modifiers to make your casual eradication of humanity a little bit easier. In game you have 3 major screens to pay attention to, your primary world map, the evolution screen and the overview. Theres little to no clutter in these screens making them easy to navigate and easy on the eyes. One recomendation I have though is to always make use of the pause time feature. It helps to plan out your next moves but keep in mind your evolution doesn't take effect until after the game is unpaused.
All in all I love this gae and am honestly suprised it's still listed as early access since it feels like a finished product. I highly recomend this game, easily worth the $15 price tag.

I am a fan of the original king of fighters installments, I had the original Neo Geo cartridge system in the mid 90's and started off with Nam, World Heroes, then Art of Fighting 1+2, Fatul Fury and additional installments of world hereos and samurai showdown. King of fighters was a good game when it first came out, and several installments on the platform saw more characters, levels and overall content. Now, King of Fighters 95 did cost me £250 all those years ago, but, the hours me and my friends put in were worth every penny. To be honest, there have been so many rehashes of king of fighters over the years on the original machine, CD and handheld as well as other platforms, and to be honest I think it has lost it's way.
I bought this expecing it to be a modern remake with enhancements, and with all of the positive reviews hoping it to be faithful to the original with fantastic sprites and sounds with upscaled visuals, whilst they tried they unfortunately fell short by quite a bit. I have no idea what game others are looking at that are saying it looks beautiful, I bought the game based on some of those reviews and I can only assume they have never played another 2D neo game before. The fonts and some of the stages / backgrounds look nice and detailed, but the main part - the characters look very washed out compared to it all, almost like you are playing at half the native resolution of your screen, and have a monitor with colour issues.
I've not played it much at all, I just thought I would go back to it to see if I could get back into it but honestly I just can't stand the blurry, milky characters, terrible bosses and other things.
You are better off just grabbing a neo emulator and playing the originals if you miss them, or perhaps getting one of those X's off of ebay, since most of the original consoles have all died by now. I've still yet to see anything that touches the original platforms titles, so I guess I am off hunting on ebay...
Sadly, dissapointed.

Papers please is a communist border guard simulation game where the player must admit or deny civilians. Players must check and double check papers provided by the people seeking admittance.
The core gameplay of papers please relies on the players perception of the paperwork itself. Players must examine each paper to confirm authenticity of provided forms including, passports, work forms, entry permits and identifications. The player will have to keep a sharp eye out for things like forged documents, discrepancies in information, expired documents and potential smugglers.
Papers please has an extremely rich story, with 20 different possible endings. These endings can be achieved depending on the players decisions in certain situations. The story revolves around a revolution brewing in the country and the player can choose to help or hinder said revolution in various ways.
Papers please does a lot right:
Fantastic story
Easy achievements
Well designed gameplay
Humble but effective art and sound design
Papers please does a few things wrong:
Can become boring
Can be considered hard for some
The game could end abruptly from one of the many endings
Papers please is a fantastic story driven "casual" game. For the price of $10.99CND it's a good price to those gamers who enjoy a good story with solid but relaxed gameplay.

The main story revolves around lead character Wei Shen. He is a police officer for the HKPD and is tasked with infiltrating the Triad gang, The Sun On Yee. The story splits between police missions and Triad missions, with individual free roam missions, favours, races, collectibles scattered throughout the map. The amount of things you can do in the game is great. From hacking cameras, setting up bugs, drug busts, martial arts training, collecting items, buying clothes and cars, betting on cockfights, playing Mahjong, driking tea and eating so many types of street food, slow motion shooting and action hijacks and even going out and signing karaoke.
The story is full of twists, betrayals and just a great narrative. That much so the awesome Donnie Yen has been recruited and a Sleeping Dogs film is in the works for 2018. (please don't mess it up)
The first story-driven game expansion, Nightmare in North Point. Its theme is based on Chinese horror and folklore, and features Chinese vampires known as the Jiangshi. In the expansion's plot, Shen's girlfriend is abducted by the ghost of Smiley Cat, a former gangster killed by Uncle Po, who has risen up from the underworld as a ghost to take his vengeance on the Sun On Yee.
2-4 hours more gameplay added with this DLC.
(100% time not just story)
A fun story which has you fighting other worldly creatures with powered up martial arts and ancient weapons.
The second story-based expansion, The Zodiac Tournament. The expansion adds a new island to the game, with new fight arenas, enemies, bosses and outfits. In the expansion's story, Shen is invited to an exclusive fighting tournament held away from Hong Kong.
The whole game plays like a 70's Bruce Lee film. Really cool nostalgic feel to it. Quite short however maybe only 1-3 hours here. (100% time not just story)
The third and final story-based expansion, Year of the Snake. It adds six missions set after the game's story. The additional missions feature Shen investigating terror attacks around Hong Kong stemming from a cultist group who believe that they will achieve spiritual salvation through the cleansing of Hong Kong residents.
After Shens exploits he has been demoted back to a beat officer. Then all hell breaks loose with a terrorist plot and you find yourself back in the thick of it straight away. This expansion is based on police work. Roughly 2-3 hours addition here. (100% time not just story)
This was a very enjoyable game. I would recommened it to fans of games like GTA, Batman Arkham and fans of crime games and martial arts in general.

Factorio....
I was a man with no money so I cracked it, and then I realized the effort given to this game.
"Its only 20$?!?!?!"
"Why haven't i bought this"
- You build a factory
- Defend it from Aliens
Sounds boring?
Yes?
Well check this out (Copy and pasted from the website)
This is the current content, some may be added and some may be changed
This is the core of the game. Mining drills digging the ground for minerals. Robotic arms moving material from one side to another. Lines of furnaces smelting the precious ores. Assembling Machines automatically building further products. And conveyor belts literally everywhere.
So you have all these machines, but they don't run for free. You need to make enough electricity to power them up. Will you go for cheap steam, that makes tons of pollution or expensive but eco friendly solar?
You are clever and skilfull. But you don't know everything out of the box. Research the technologies to make your way up the tree to completely automated and self sufficient factories.
There is more to the production than just minerals. This planet is rich in oil as well. And you will need it. Pump it from the dephts. Break it to fractions in Oil Refineries and put it to good use in Chemical plants.
Belts are great for minerals. If the mineral fields are close. And not that big. Otherwise you better build good-old train tracks and scale your logistics to a new level.
The "third support" of the logistic system. You need advanced technology for this. But once you have it you have all these cool looking drones that move the stuff for you based on some general conditions you set up.
Tired of manually building another mining site. Just use a blueprint. Define what should be built, provide the material and a bunch of building drones will build the whole thing for you.
You want to have exactly 1006 circuits in your buffers? No problem, just make a signal that switches off the production line once you have reached the limit. This is advanced but powerful concept where you can really "program" your factory. It will be expanded even more in the near future.
You are not welcome on this planet. With all your smokey machines that generate plenty of waste and destroy the environment. If you make too much pollution you better prepare for the enraged natives to come after you.
Those natives are really annoying, aren't they? You need to build walls and turrets to protect from their rage attacks. But wait, there is a plenty of military options for you to "solve the situation". The fight mechanics are at the moment weaker compared to the rest of the content (which is quite mature). We will work on this.
The main singleplayer game requires a lot of work to finish. The task is simple, build the silo, build the rocket and launch a satellite into space. You will need to do your best to achieve this goal. On top of that every game is a different challenge because of our procedural map generation.
The Scenario pack is a set of additional mini campaigns. At the moment there are three, but we plan to add more in the future.
Factorio is designed from the beginning to be highly moddable. Most of the game data are stored in the Lua data files and can be changed by the mods. Mods can also change behavior of the running game via modding scripts, also written in Lua language.
The game has a custom built in map editor. We used it to make all the campaign and scenario maps. It is there for you to make new content for the game. You can also attach a Lua script to the map and make a challenge scenario with specific set of rules.
Build the factory with your buddies. Or just visit a game of your friends and let him show you around. At the moment the rough version of the Multiplayer is working and people are enjoying mostly co-op games. We will look it more user friendly in the near future.

I like to leave legitimate reviews for games, despite how "serious" the game is.  So this review will be no different.
If you remember AIM (AOL Instant Messenger), then you will feel the nostalgia bomb the minute you start the game for the first time.  That's mostly the reason why I got this, aside from the obvious laugh (and easy 100% achievement).
The plot is basically that you are a dude in his senior year of high school, and he clearly likes this girl named Emily, which he talks to regularly on AIM.
The interaction itself is Emily writing a message to you on AIM, and then you choosing 1,2 or 3 on your keyboard, which correlate to different responses.  The chapters are based on years, so while you start in your senior year of high school, you progress until your senior year of college before the game ends.
The "game story" itself is linear.  You can get different responses based on the choices you make, but at the end of college, the result is always the same.  And it's quite a sad ending, to be honest.
The game is free to play, so obviously you really don't need to be reading reviews.  It's an enjoyable experience mixed in with some nostalgia and some other feels.  I recommend it based on all of the things mentioned in this review.
Kudos to the game creator, Kyle Seeley, for taking the time and effort to put together a nifty little point and click experience for all of us that came from that era of the Internet.
I, for one, will always remember the many years I spent on AIM.  Growing up, posting lyrics away messages and adding quotes to my profile so I could look cool to everybody else.
Download this game and enjoy the feels of 2002 all over again.
----
As for the achievements: once you complete the game, you can go back and start the first "Chapter" again.  Enter "Password123" as your screen name and then anything as your name.  It will unlock all of the icons you need to use to get all of the achievements.
From there, just select the icon, engage in brief conversation with Emily until she acknowledges your icon.  At that point, the achievement will be unlocked.
Repeat the first year again and again with the same screen name as I mentioned to get all of the achievements.
