I see too much hate thrown at this game honestly. Sure it might've been short, but so were the classic Sonic Games that we love so much. Short games are not an issue to me, as long as I'm enjoying the experience, and with Bubsy I certaintly did.
This is by far the best Bubsy Game out there. It looks back at what went wrong in the past games, and makes it work. The One-Hit Kill was the cheapest thing ever in the original game as you went too fast, and the camera was too close to Bubsy. In this game, you still die by one-hit, but you can pickup a shield in every level almost anywhere, you move at a normal speed for a Platformer, and the levels are build AROUND the One-Hit deaths so that you become more cautious, leaving every death you encounter to be your own fault, which is exactly what a game should do.
In my opinion, I think people are giving this game way too much hate. Not every game is going to be a perfect Gold X Award that you will enjoy, and I honestly think some of you were expecting too much from this new game. All I expected was it to have Bubsy, and to fix what the other games did wrong. I can safely say, that all my expectations were fulfilled.
I played this with my friend during a stream, and we were laughing, having fun, and just outright amazed by how much we liked the game. It's not Game of the Year Material at all, but it is definitely a gateway for Bubsy to finally return for more Modern Games.
It's great to have you back Bobcat. The 20 years was worth the wait.
PS: The soundtrack is also very catchy. Much better than whatever they tried to do in the last games.

$30 for less than 2 hours of content that wasn't even fully playtested and lazily constructed. Expect bosses to glitch out. Expect cheap deaths. Pointless collecting that serves absolutely no purpose. None. There are goals in the levels that do NOT affect your progress. There are keys to collect, and you collect them all to collect more wool. What do you do with the wool? Nothing. They don't add anything. They don't unlock anything AFAIK. I'm not willing to replay this to find out.
Controls that are mediocre at best, and sometimes just frustratingly bad. The pounce gets you killed because you completely lose control of the character once it's used.
Nothing memorable or funny happens. At all. The levels are just generic assets. You could replace the characters with anything and you wouldn't even know this was supposed to be a Bubsy game. They're not wacky looking or even full of weird quirky characters like the other games. They're just boring, and full of the same recolored enemies. Over and over for about 10 levels. There are 3 bosses. Each boss is pretty much the same boss with maybe one or two new attacks. The boss fights are incredibly slow, and they also don't recover HP when you die. This is probably because you can die to them in incredibly dumb (and sometimes broken/glitched/unfair) ways and it's a lazy way to excuse just not making them actually fun encounters.
The cutscenes aren't even animated. They're just still images sliding around. That's it. Super lazy.
Bubsy has nothing remotely funny to say. Gex has wittier dialogue than this.
The levels themeatically are nothing like the rest of the series. They are very very very uninspired and I would not be shocked if they used generic assets for them.
The lighting engine is so amazingly terrible and basic. Half the time you cant even see Bubsy's face because he's obscurred by shadows -- not that it ever does anything interesting, but he is the main character. Dont get me wrong. He has no facial expressions, really. That'd require effort.
This feels like they were clearly intending for this to sell based off the "Bubsy is bad" meme alone with absolutely no effort put into making the game. If anything, it feels like they reskinned some mobile game made as someone's first attempt at being an indie developer. The price tag just makes that aspect alone feel scummy.
I'd refund this had Accolade not sent me a key for it to stream.
Overall 4/10, and a 5 at best, just because it's playable. I'd say buy this for a kid who doesn't know better as a bargain bin game to keep them occupied, but it's THIRTY DOLLARS.
THIRTY.
DOLLARS.
FOR 2 HOURS.
Whoever says this game is good or "fine" didn't actually play it themselves or understands just how scummy the devs are for making it the way it is.
I dont care if any aspect of this review is actually wrong or something. I really didn't like this.

A non sarcastic review from someone who put time into the game.
I was given Bubsy 3d as one of my first videogames back when it came out. I was 3 and so grew up playing it and so I do have a fair bit of nostalgia for the charactar despite that game being fairly terrible. That said I was stoked when I heard Bubsy was coming back, I didnt expect much. A simple platformer with decent design was all I really wanted and thats exactly what I got.
The game is short, very short. That said, those people saying its beatable in an hour or less are either not playing it right or are flat out lying. I put time into trying to get as many collectables as I could on my first playthrough up untill the last few levels and the game took me 3 hours. 3 very entertaining hours.
Platforming is responsive and works well, levels are nicely laid out if not a little too generous with checkpoints and health shirt pickups. Backgrounds however while colourful are very generic untill the final few levels, they look like something ripped out of a generic arcade shooter. Everything else however really pops, the enemies look great, bubsy looks great and the whole thing runs smoothly.
Those buying this for nostalgia towards the bobcat should note though that despite having a slider in the options to decide how much Bubsy talks the number of lines are EXTREMELY limited, He had two seperate lines that I could tell talking about Pouncing being a new skill despite it being present in Bubsy 2 im near certain.
Despite the minor nitpicks and some fps drops/graphical glitches in the final three or four levels this game is a joy to play for platformer fans, marred by a dire lack of stages however it is not worth the price it will soon be rising up to. As is id say get it before the price goes up or wait untill its on sale, hell even get it and refund it if you arent happy. You can't go wrong.
A few patches and hopefully some dlc will make this a great little gem of a platformer and a fantastic return for Bubsy the bobcat.

I've played the game for a little bit... The game is a bit traditional for an MMO, but is starting to actually branch out in many ways... I've got hope that this game could end up starting to tap into ideas that other MMOs would be afraid to try out.
The game is very story driven, which for some, may not be what they want in an MMO. But you can expect the usual FF tropes you've come to love, the over-serious moments, the heart breaking ones, the silly ones. It's kind of a grab bag of a lot of the different emotions many of the main line Final Fantasy RPG's brought to the world, but put in the form of an MMO.
Many say that this is exactly like 11, in that because it's an MMO, it doesn't deserve to have the number attached to it.. It's not a real Final Fantasy.. But, It's actually got a lot of what makes the Final Fantasy games what they are in it.
The pay to play setup seems to dissuade many, but out of the MMO's I've played (Which has been quite a few) and just games in general.. This player base for this game is relatively non-toxic. Not to say that the game doesn't have its trolls/toxic players... What game doesn't? But the pay to play helps the game to keep the player base clean, and helps the developers to push the game forward in the ways they see fit, as to rather having to take marketing and microtransactions into account.
It has content that slowly ramps up in difficulty as you go, has things in it for the casual players, the midcore players, and the extremely hardcore players as well. And it's actually pretty nice to see a game that is actually trying its best to cater to everyone's wants/needs in a game, as opposed to just saying "Deal with it." PvP is balanced in its own way, seperate from PvE altogether, so you don't get some of the issues WoW had.. And the content actually gets to being fairly difficult towards the higher difficulty raids.
Square may occasionally make some questionable choices/decisions.. And I can't say I always agree with every business decision they make.. And the deal with the DDOSing of the servers at the launch of stormblood and at every major patch released thus far are irritating. But the game has a lot of promise, and I've got hope that this game could end up being something more than it is now even.

Just finished the main story and most of the side activites. I still have some unfinished business which I'm pretty sure I will come back to.
Sleeping Dogs is in my opinion one of the most unique open world crime games out there. To be honest I enjoyed it more than all the Saints Rows for instance (even GTA 4... Don't hate me)
So, to summarize it all:

-The game looks great. It's a remaster of a game from 2012 so nothing too mindblowing! Still holds well in my opinion though.
-It's darker, grittier than GTA for instance. It's gonna get bloody a lot.
-Combat is really amazing. Most of the time you're gonna rely on kung fu which can be fun and you can learn new combos and attacks. There are also handguns, shotguns, assault rifles and you also get a cover system to use. Firearms don't really feel unique but vaulting over cover while you're shooting up gangsters in slowmo makes 'em fun to use.
-Hong Kong is alive. The environment is detailed, you can see people in stores, in parks chilling on benches, talking and that kind of stuff.  Basically it feels like wandering in a huge metropolis so that's a plus.
-Lots of side content: There are races, side missions which fill up your "Face lever" and gives you ingame bonuses, opens up content. Lots of missions as well.
-Variety of vehicles, clothes, food to eat (gives you temporary buffs)
-Simple but interesting story and main character. I also liked the ending which is considered "meh" by many people
-Good voice acting
-Has all the DLC.

-It can be repetitive. The side content is the main culprite here. There are a few "do this for me a hundred million times" kind of side missions. Luckily not too many.
-Simple story. Plot twists can be obvious sometimes. Still liked it though
-(Personal opinion here):In my opinion it would have been cooler if the devs have used the chinese language more. Some people speak chinese in the game but it's not enough.
-Minor graphical bugs
Overall: I thoroughly enjoyed Sleeping Dogs. This was actually my third time finishing the game (first one on Steam). I think you can have at least 12-15 hours of fun with the game without the side content but let's face it: It's an open world game! You wanna do side stuff don't you?
So yes! I absolutely recommend Sleeping Dogs if you're looking for an original, stylish open world game. I hope that most of you are going to enjoy it as much as I did!

The basic premise of Legend of Grimrock is that it is a modern take on the classic grid-based,dungeon-crawling,RPG games of old, like Dungeon Master, Eye of the Beholder etc. You start out with a party of 4 adventurers (arranged in a 2x2 formation)... in this case convicted as criminals and thrown into a secure prison.. and must explore the prison/dungeon to learn its secrets and find a way out. Movement is directional, plus rotate left and right, around a series of 2 dimensional grid based levels. There are various monsters to fight and puzzles to solve in order to progress through the game. Fighting is done by means of clicking on the items equipped in your characters' hands, often whilst performing a "Square dance" with the monsters to avoid letting them hit your party
The graphics have been updated, especially the lighting engine, which is amazing, but repeating textures are still used widely, and the gameplay itself is very reminiscent of the early games. Objects are interacted with by click on the screen e.g. to press a button or open a door and items can be picked up and carried/used by your party of adventurers. The adventurers attack by left-clicking the items that are placed in their hands, and spells can be cast by choosing the right combination of runes for a spell the adventurer has learnt.
There are 4 races:- Humans; Minotaurs; Lizardmen; and Insectoids, and 3 character classes - Fighter; Mage; Rogue. and you can either play with a default party, or create one of your own.
According to Steam I have racked up 410 hours of playing time on Legend of Grimrock... mostly that is because a dungeon editor was released and I have spent a huge amount of time working on my own creations. I have however also completed the main game at least 3 times. Firstly with a hand-picked party of 4 characters, then again with a special unlockable solo character, and finally a hard,old-school playthrough with no automap. I've also spent a large amount of time using the Dungeon Editor and writing scripts to create my own levels/puzzles/spells etc. My first play through took 19 hours 35 minutes of playing time, which took 26 hours in total according to steam (including re-loads and breaks).
Overall.. I used to love the old DM/EOB games and I absolutely love this modern take... And what's even better is that the designers continued to support their creation by giving the modding community a brilliant dungeon editor that allowed those of us with an interest to exert our creative muscles.
This is a fantastic throwback to the old gold box and wizardry games. Grimrock has fantastic graphics, engaging real-time combat and just the right depth of character creation and progression.
A fun dungeon crawl for the hardcore RPG fans. Satisfied all my nostalgia for the old Dungeon Master game!
Great fun!

Legend of Grimrock is one of those games, that seemed, at least for the most of us, to have come out of nowhere.
It puts one goal in it's mind - to recreate the old school dungeon crawler "Dungeon Master; Eye of the Beholder" style games. And Ladies and Gentlemen - it does that very, very well.
The game is engaging, interesting and challenging. It does not try to be what it is not, nor it is any pretentious in any sort of way. The developer team knew his limits, budgets and skills and used that to a supreme extend. No, seriously - the game looks highly polished and finished, well balanced in all manner of presentation. It is a great skill to distribute your resources like that so you achieve a lot, using something modest.
As for the game itself - it is a 4 person party hex based, 1st person, real time, dungeon crawler. It takes the best from the old school similar games and improves that using today's technology and UI.
Of course, to be objective - it is not a game for each style. The combat is a combination of tactics and quick reflexes, using the mouse and keyboard at the same time. It may take some time to get used to it, but once you are used to it - it's getting exciting.
The only criticism of the game itself is that the final boss battle, the first time it is played, has this unbalanced feeling that each wrong move leads to your death. When this happens for 10th+ time, it can really get on your nerves. Basically - each mistake is a death there. The good point is, once you figure the stuff out - the boss becomes far easier.
As a final though - I recommend this game as it is a very well executed product. If you are going to take it though, please, watch some gameplay videos first to see if it really is for you. As I said - the game is pretty good, just not for everyone.
Legend of Grimrock 2 is in the works. The team had great sales thus they can continue their indie work. We can expect the next game to be even better, with significantly bigger budget.

Every now and then there comes a game that tries to revisit genres that have fallen by the wayside as the video game industry continues to change and grow. Dungeon crawler games, for the most part, happen to be one of those genres. So when I first saw images for Legend of Grimrock I couldn’t help but be excited.
When I was a kid I spent a lot of time playing the old dungeon crawler games. I still vividly remember such titles as Dungeon Master and Dungeon Master II: The Legend of Skullkeep. Given how much time I spent playing those games, and loving every minute of it, I was hoping that this new game would live up to the games in whose footsteps it was following.
I’ll tell you right now, I have not been disappointed.
Legend of Grimrock is everything it is supposed to be. It is an old-style dungeon crawler modernized for today’s gaming world. While such a game can be limited in terms of graphics and art style, Almost Human, the indie developer behind the title, has executed it perfectly. The game looks great and the various creatures’ appearances are fantastic given the limits of the genre.

Probably one of the best made games out there. Hand-painted levels, characters, and assets. Incredible and above all believable voice acting. The SOUNDTRACK is incredible, worth buying alongside the game. All of these facets have had some serious Supergiant Love™ put into them, and they all combine to provide an incredibly dense, atmospheric game. I can't describe what playing this game feels like, but I think you'll understand once the humming kicks in. Ashley Barrett's voice does wonders for this game, and her vocals alongside Darren Korb's instrumentals are a gift from God.
But enough about that. The gameplay is very different from Supergiant's previous game, Bastion. Armed with a cyberpunk version of the Buster Sword you can either engage in something vaguely similar to Bastion's combat in real-time, or go into a tactical planning mode, which allows you to pause the game and plan out complex attack patterns and movement. There are so many abilities in this game, and every single one can be combined with another to make what might as well be a different ability, with different effects depending on which slot you put them in.
The combat is deep, and the only problem I have with it is that most people won't bother to experiment as much as you can in this game, as you can get quite far with very basic setups. I think Supergiant could have introduced enemies that were only or more vulnerable to certain chains or types of attacks.
I won't talk about the story too much, but I will say that it's good and you really end up caring about Red and her companion. There isn't ANY exposition rammed down your throat, and you find more about the world from optional terminals and areas. These do a good job, and the story will ensure that your tears will be streaming at the end. It's nothing ground-breaking, but it's executed with such style and it oozes Supergiant's trademark charm.
In short, BUY THIS GAME. Supergiant have yet to make a game short of excellency, and while it's not a long game, clocking in at about 10 hours, those 10 hours are some of the best you'll have playing video games.

Steel division is a strategy based game and it's a real good one; for those who already know the company that made the game you won't be disapointed, you'll find almost the same mecanics that run wargame red dragon, airland batlles and european escalation.
What's is slightly different in this game is that a game is divided in three phases: in the first phase you'll basically have no heavy support and you'll got to rely on light armament that arrived firts on the field while heavier machines will arrive later.
The other difference is that you no longer have areas to conquer and defend, now the whole map is cut in two: you're side and the ennemy's side, this front will extend when you're units move forward and naturally you're area will decrease as long as the ennemy move towards you or destroy you're units.
Except that the game is like wargame but in the WWII era, the deck system where you chose the units that you'll be able to bring on the field is still there even if you can bring far less units than you were used to in wargame; for exemple you won't be able to bring dozens of tanks, some powerfull units are particularly rare and you might take care of them.
For those who are new to strategy games or at least this kind of strategy, the game is pretty hard and "realistic", you'll have to practice but once you've got the hang of it you'll find a most satisfying game.

-Work in Progress-
The movement is way too gamey for lugging around a hulking rig and exoskeleton.. Its too quick, and has zero momentum.. Its instant full speed, instant turning on a dime, no slow down, nothing.. I personally think Lords of the Fallen was superior in combat..
Once you get to the second area, you start fighting guys wearing Rhino armor, Ive noticed one o two who seem to teleport a bit.. Most notably, the guy with the one handed fire sword (similar moveset to the chainsaw).. The enemies using faster weapons, or dual wielding have almost no telegraph, and have perfect tracking, which becomes annoying.. Whenever Im fighting a Rhino guy, with a fastw eapon, its garanteed Im swapping blows..
The healing mechanic SUCKS... Allow me to elaborate.. You use injectors, which would be fine, except that there are multiple tiers, and then other items to inject.. Such as damage boosts, heal over times, elemental damage boosts, etc.. And theres only ONE key to heal.. Meaning during the heat of battle, you have to tap the right directional key, until you get to the one you need.. They have tiny icons, and it takes your thumb off of the left analog, which you need to move.. There is a kindve positive, depending on what kind of player you are.. They cannot be used while in attack animations, and cannot be spammed (small cooldown).. This makes perfect sense for potions, but these are injectors, attached to your bdy.. Its not like you have to stop, pop a cork, and chug.. I played from a controller, and its likely better on m+kb in this aspect, but I prefer analogs and triggers for this style of game..
I got it on sale, and recommend even at full price.. Its definitely fun, but is not without some minor issue.. I liked Lords of the Fallen.. Aside from its poor technical issues at release, I dont understand the flak it gets.. Though admittedly, i did have problems with its claims that enemies follow the same rules as the player.. They had no issue beginning a combo on you, while you were mid combo, staggering the ever loving shiitt out of them... Also a poor camera.. Which, persists in The Surge.
-UPDATE/Final Assessment-
After 70 hrs or so, and a 2nd character at rank 80, I absolutely adore this game.. However.. I now see the disdain for the final map, the Nucleus.. It is a maze, which I enjoy, but the blob enemies suck.. Not because theyre hard, but because theyre glitchy, and its sometimes impossible to tell which attack theyre doing, and even more difficult to tell how far away the attacks land.. Sometimes the long arms will remain visually, so it looks like it has permanent tree limbs sticking out 4 times its length. There are also FAR too many of them!  Some areas have 2, or 1 and a Chrysalid enemy.. Other than the terrible blob enemies, I have less complaints..
Still has camera issues however, but the combat is top notch.. Possibly better than any other game!  Hitboxes are superb(Except for staff enemies.. Theyre broken), and input is crisp.. You will have no issue with movement control in this game(though I thought it could use more weight/momentum in movement.. Somewhere between this, and LotF).. Except for the ridiculous jump/duck mechanic tied to blocking.. It usually doesnt work in combat, and is clunky as hell.. The map layout is awesome, although somewhat samey made better by the dlc which break it up.. Its understandable from a lore standpoint, as its all in the same factory.. The weapons and armor are pretty cool as well, and the level up system is simple, but effective.. I never really tired of fighting enemies, as they made a smart way of having to farm the upgrade mats and gear itself.. Works surprisingly well, and allowed for longer play before fatigue of enemy set in.. The small amount of boss battles is a shame, but the combat throughout makes up for it, as the normal enemies are always deadly, and make up for the lack of boss battles.. Implants do make for some differences in build, but there is no build diversity Im sorry to say.. Heavy gear, or light gear have minor differences, and implants add a little more, but all in all, each will play the same..
I enjoyed Lords of the Fallen, but I have to agree that this is leaps and bounds better! A must have for any 3rd person action rpg fan!
Edit: NG+ changed my mind.. There are new enemies, and they hit for FAR too much damage.. A staff wielder in the very beginning for example.. 170-200 dmg per attack, and has up to 6 hit combos.. Carbon Cat, is hitting me for almost 500dmg if I take on of his bigger hits.. I like a challenge, but the damage is tuned TOO high..

Playing through the Surge has been one of the most enjoyable gaming experiences I have had to date. Everyone knows it's a souls like game but it is much more than that at heart.
It's easy to brush off the story at play here but I urge everyone to actually pay attention. Listen to the audiologs. Explore everything. Do the side quests. It's hard for a game like this - not focused on story but focused around it's difficulty and core gameplay loops to engage you in a thought out story, and while I admit it wasn't the best told tale it was certainly an interesting one. There are plenty of seemingly pointless audio logs or focus points that will all be revealed later on in the game and all of them will open your eyes to how grim the world of the Surge really is. Had it been a little more polished and perhaps given some background lore this would have been one of the best stories in gaming, in my opinion.
Aside from my love of the story, the game has many selling points.
- The combat is very, very satisfying. Yes it recycles the core dark souls style but it adds to it and IMO improves on it. With execution moves and pinpoint targeting you really feel in control in the fights you get into. The actual difficulty in fighting enemies I feel was greater than any other souls like game I have played (DS1,2 and 3) and I initially it a serious wall in combat. Practice truly does make perfect though and the game will reward you for trying again, because once you get the hang of your preferred weapon (of which there are tonnes) and can learn off some enemy move sets you'll be making your way through enemies like greased lighting.
-Customization is also plentiful. The Surge doesn't let you sink EXP points into any given skills or any of those familiar rpg mechanics you may be used to, but instead it has its very unique implant system. These implants allow you to drastically change up your playstyle and as you progress further into the game and find more you can adapt and overcome most situations. All of these implants rely on your core power which is in essence the exp sink of the game, but it doesn't increase your base stats, and will only allow you to add more implants or equip more powerful gear. It was an odd system to me when I first started but I like what they have done. I can choose to go into a fight stacked with HP implants and healing implants, or I can throw caution to the wind and only take DPS implants. High risk high reward gameplay is ever present in the Surge and the implant system simply puts the cherry on top.
-The game is gorgeous. Now I realize it is set indoors in familiar environments like 80% of the time but my god are those environments well done. The textures are beautiful and everything looks perfect. There are some sections when you walk through tunnels and I personally had to stop and admire my character model during some of these instances when the light hit me a certain way. It's easy to say that everything in the game looks the same because they're all robots and everything is mechanical etc. But looking similar doesn't mean looking bad.
-There are plenty of nifty little things that make the game so much more enjoyable. Set bonuses, secret areas, collectibles, easter eggs, ironic humour and more.
There is an abundance of things to do in the NG mode and then plenty of farming and upgrades and extra goodies in NG+, there is a DLC that just came out too so you won't be stuck for content in the slightest. Any souls fan is missing out big time if they pass up on this game, even if the setting doesn't appeal to you I urge you to try it because it will grow on you and you will love it.
10/10. I really don't have a bad word to say about this game. Say for the music that plays in the OPS centers, but that's so minimal it really doesn't matter.

The team behind Lords of the Fallen have another go at the souls-like genre, and it's a better game fullstop. It's actually more like Bloodborne than Dark Souls as the combat is faster paced with an emphasis on dodging, and trying to tank anything will result in a swift(er) demise. Yes, it's a challenging game, punishing even but never unfair and the progress feels just right.
Combat is good, with everything feeling meaty. It's also fairly unique that the gear and weapons you get are mainly sourced from cutting them from enemies. Upgrades require more parts, so do you go for that armoured chest on the enemy or the unarmoured head? The formers rewards are higher but comes with greater risk. It's a nice system with plenty of scope for different builds and playstyles.
The futuristic/apocalyptic setting is very well done and the visuals are excellent, with great animations and sharp texturing. The sound is also top notch, and you can even add your own music to the Ops centres, these are your basic hubs throughtout the game where you can upgrade parts and implants and take a breather. The level design is also very well done, however the game doesn't hold your hand what so ever so it can feel maze like at first. Size wise, it's a big game. Not the biggest but it still took me 45hrs to complete, and i missed some side quests/items which i'm going to do in NG+.
The 'Walk in the Park' dlc is also excellent, with a really different setting to the rest of the game, adds some really nice touches (you can have a go on a rollercoaster!) and it's also woven into the main game perfectly. So i recommend buying the complete pack for the full experience. Great game. I highly recommend The Surge.

Legend of Grimrock is a modern looking version of the old dungeon crawling genre.
What is dungeon crawling? You might ask, well a dungeon crawler is a first person game where you play as an adventurer, or usually a party of adventurers that delve into dungeons, level up and complete quests, what makes dungeon crawlers so much different from modern RPG's  is that dungeon crawlers often use complex puzzles in their level design, making it more of a puzzle game than a grindfest.
The game starts you off with a standard party of four characters that work well together, but you can create your own party of course!
The characters you play are outcast by society and have to fight for their lives to have their crimes abolished on the mountain of Grimrock.
The game looks simply gorgeous for a game in it's genre, even on my terrible terrible laptop it runs very smooth at the maximum graphical settings.
The combat system is a bit like the old Final Fantasy/Chrono Trigger combat system mixed in with the Dungeon Master/Shin Megami Tensei combat, you can move about freely in a grid of squares, while your attacks aren't turnbased, they just have cooldowns.
The challenge this game holds is above average, don't expect to blaze through it on your first playthrough, nonetheless it's a great game overall!
The puzzles don't let you get stuck for a long time, they're quite clear about what needs to be done, which is a good thing in my opinion.
I could whole-heartedly recommend you this title if you want to play a casual game with a decent bit of challenge, especially when it's on sale, then it's definately worth the money.
If you're on the fence about this game, I'd say go and buy it, if you weren't interested before, this probably isn't your type of game, and I'd recommend you watching a let's play.

After 47 hours, I finally beat the base game. And... I'm torn. On one hand... this is a great souls-like game. On the other hand... it leaves much to be desired.
Pros:
-Cutting off an enemy's armor. It's a unique combat feature that pretty much ensures that you always get 'drops' from enemies. AND, they contribute to you leveling progress. It's such a simple and fantastic idea.
-Story and art design. While it may not be as thought provoking and visually striking as the Dark Souls series, it's still well done. Hell, just the idea of nanomachines + exo-rigs essentially zombifying people... it's a fascinating thought.
-Storing scrap. Probably the one thing I can say this game actually did better than Dark Souls.
Cons:
-NPCs are kind of lacking. You can do a few things with NPCs, and that's great... but their interactions are, for the most part, slightly boring. Only one of them shows any signs of personality.
-Clunky, often frustrating combat. Yes, I know, we play these games for the challenge. But there is so much to the combat that needs fine-tuning. Inaccurate hitboxes. Inputs don't respond during enemy attacks sometimes, even though you aren't staggered. Enemy lunge attacks sometimes push around corners, and despite their slowed momentum still hit you for massive amounts of damage (I'm looking at you, you four legged ♥♥♥♥s).
-One particularly complex boss fight, which had an unnecessarily obscure mechanic to it.
-Level design. Don't get me wrong, I loved the art in this game. But... my God... I got lost so many times. Lifts were used way too often in attempts to create complex pathing within a single area. While I appreciate the thoughtfullness of adding in multiple shortcuts to help the player along, I ultimately ended up running around in circles trying to find my next objective.
-Traveling hurts. This goes along with the previous note. There's no universal travel system, just a tram/door which takes you from one area to the next. Yes, the shortcuts helped loop you back around to the safety of an OPS station (this games version of a 'bonfire')... however... there were so many different paths per 'level'... I would often find myself at an OPS stations trying to remember which direction I came from, and how to get back on the right path.
-TIMED SCAP COLLECTION. I can't tell you how much progress I've lost because I've died at the end of a stupidly long path and couldn't get back to my scrap in time. This last time, upwards of 200k all at once. It was sitting right by a shortcut door, which could only be opened from that side. This mechanic has no reason to exist other than to frustrate the player.
Final say:
This game started out so strong. The concept is solid, but the execution... well... it could use more polish. There are just too many flaws to ignore. It's not Dark Souls. Then again, I never expected it to be.
It's not a must-buy. But if you're a fan of the genre, I think you should still check it out.
------------------------------
DLC and NG+
Okay, let me just say this first: The art design is much improved over the base game. Level design still leaves something to be desired, but just visually the DLC stands out.
With that being said, the core game design and mechanics still hurt... and not in a good way. Artificial difficulty spikes are much more apparent in NG+. The inconsistency of enemy attack power, and... well... just combat in general... is really disheartening. If you've kept up on your leveling and gear management, no single enemy should be able to one-shot you.
Let me say that again.
If you've kept up with your leveling and gear management.... No. Single. Enemy. Should. Be. Able. To. One. Shot. You.
In a nutshell, that's the difference between 'difficult' and 'punishing'. I'm a patient man. I've made my way through some intense and challenging boss fights in other games. I couldn't even finish fighting the final DLC Boss because it was just so idioticly unforgiving. It didn't just kill me, it killed all the fun out of this game for me.
Final-final say: I've changed my mind. I'm not going to call the game out-right♥♥♥♥♥♥ But... yeah. I'm no longer recommending this game. If you're a fan of the Dark Souls genre, proceed with caution.

Fans of old school CRPGs like Dungeon Master and the original Wizardry series will get their money's worth out of Legend of Grimrock. Traps, puzzles, hidden caches of treasure, resource management, multiple character team... it's all here. Challenging and unforgiving, Legend of Grimrock will teach you early to tread cautiously and save often.
The game includes a dungeon editor and built-in mod support, and the LoG player community is truly incredible.

Wizardry, Bards Tale, Dragon Wars, Eye of the Beholder... I have fond memories of all those games. The developers of "Legend of Grimrock" hoped to tap into that nostalgia with their new RPG, which updated the graphics but retained the retro gameplay. Unfortunately, they failed to take into account that there is a reason I don't play those games anymore: that retro gameplay sucks.
Even back in the day, I hated the ridiculous maze-like levels and the "find the hidden button" puzzles, and looking for keys to open the next area is a trope so old that even Duke Nukem made fun of it. The combat is mildly entertaining, but - having long mastered the attack/strafe techniques in the early '90s - it lacks challenge. A distinct lack of variety in monsters and textures made it hard to maintain interest. I think I'll stick to more modern games in future.

Excellent game, i devoured it from start to finish only to find myself wanting to replay it (you can keep your char and replay it at a higher difficulty). The entire time you're playing it you don't know what world you're into, as it happens in "hardcore" sci fi generally, as if it's so advanced that it makes little sense. This battle system is AMAZING. I had played a game with such a battle system (a platformer with a ninja or something though i don't remember the name - that game however was poorly made) and i was wondering why such a battle system was never implemented anywhere else. To all that read this review, i have to tell you what i mean by that: you plan your moves beforehand and the character excecutes them all in some sort of bullet-time event. I have to say this because i didn't know it personally, i only got the game because of the positive reviews and the sci fi feel (i love sci fi rpgs).
This game is artistic, which means that its largest advantage is its scenario/atmosphere. What an amazing feeling. The sword speaks the words that the protagonist can't, while sensual/sad music (similar to portishead) plays in the background. This whole "noir" story develops while you try to find answers by advancing, installing new functions or upgrades, using new limiters. And every time the sword speaks about what you're reading and what you're doing complimenting the already excellent reading material. The story never gets boring and you never need to "grind" (the tests cannot be considered "grinding" since they are one-timers). What you need is to get better and plan more strategically.
The functions (skills) are all different and can all be used as active,passive or to even upgrade other functions and then can be rearranged for different results. (What do i mean by that, let's give a simple example: you have a skill that strikes for some damage. You have a skill that seeks the enemy and does dot. So if you upgrade the first skill with the second skill then the first skill also does dot by itself.)
What can i say? Noir atmosphere, amazing music, captivating story, excellent combat system, diverse skills, without grinding or asking for more money, this game has everything. I bought it on sale but it's really worth its money anyway. I've never finished a game to then be as excited to replay it.
So we've covered the positives. The negatives are very few but there are some.
First of all, at some battles if your character remains at a specific corner the enemies won't chase her (this happened three times, and it's ok in the normal battles since you will eventually have to defeat them so it doesn't really matter, but it also happened during a survival test - i passed the test by positioning my char at a corner that noone could see her).
Secondly at some battles you don't know it but you won't get xp for finishing them (the game wants you (and even tells you) to skip them but if you do them anyway you aren't rewarded) - i would prefer those to be "properly" unbeatable, as if the enemy has a specific armor that you can't remove and which negates all damage or that the enemy is completely untargettable. This happened only twice in the game (and actually you already kind of know that you won't get any xp but you try anyway).
Thirdly in some cases the sword was talking because of the storyline progression and as he was talking i pressed to observe something and i basically lost the dialogue for what i was observing. I felt that twice or three times towards the end.
Fourth, in some cases the game would not play that well, as if it was overwhelmed with graphics. I don't know if that makes much sense. Although my graphics card is obviously not the best, it does cover a lot more than the minimum requirements but i still got some cases of "laggy" instances. By that i mean that the world did not feel as smooth as in other areas. This happened frequently but it's mostly due to my graphics card i guess.
In these "negatives" i specifically said how many times it happened because i wanted the readers to know that even these happen once or twice in the entire game. The game is almost literally a masterpiece. It's like reading a book but you're actually playing it. It's awesome. I honestly didn't expect this to be that good. But it is.
So my advice to all of you who are even mildly interested is to buy it straight away. It is a finished game that has a lot of replayability and never feels buggy or unfinished or boring. And right now it's up for sale for 4 euros, it's silly not to get it. But it's even worth its original price of 19 euros.

Plague Inc is a rather satisfying simulation in which the player's goal is to infect and kill off the entire world. Just exactly how the player chooses to tackle this is up to them.
Gameplay
The player can choose to slowly infect the population, remaining undetected and non-lethal, and then strike once much of the world's population is infected by evolving lethality to kill fast and unexpectedly, making it difficult for the world to react and cure it in time or just try to kill the world as fast as possible which usually results in losing the game as many of the more isolated countries such as Greenland will shut their ports and airports making it very difficult to infect them.
Content
The player is not presented with just one disease type, but many. These disease types range from a neurax worm which allows the player to manipulate infected hosts to their advantage to the necroa virus which allows the player to unleash a devastating zombie apocalypse on the world. It doesn't stop here though as there is a rather extensive community workshop with countless unique diseases thanks to the scenario creator which is available to every player who owns the game.
More coming
The developers of this game are also working on a multiplayer mode which will see two players battle it out to see who's plague is superior. The game is also regularly updated with new content and bug fixes.
Conclusion
While Plague Inc is not perfect, it offers great replayability with different ways to beat different scenarios and higher difficulty modes which can really challenge the player. The price is rather steep so I would suggest waiting until the game is on sale to get the best value for money. 8/10 - Great game.

All things considered, the game isn't 'bad'. Not good, but okay. I've only completed the first set of levels so I can't account for the whole game in writing this, but I have read other reviews here so I wish to factor that in.
Honestly as far as length goes this feels like "Sonic 4 - Episode 1 (or Sonic 2 in some ways). Similar repetition, but it also feels like there's actually less uniqueness within levels and (yes I dare say this) charm than the very first game. The first game offered some interesting level design choices and had some interesting gimmicks mixed in. This one just has a lot of the same, and with floating stationary bad guys everywhere for the purpose of convenient platforming (akin to the Bubbles badnicks in Sonic 4 Ep 1).
The pounce attack is a nice idea, Bubsy's jump height seems smaller than ever (one of the gripes with the controls there), he otherwise controls pretty well. The presentation is actually better than I thought compared with what I expected from the trailer. The glow effect on the yarn balls is a bit much and lacks a bit of detail compared to say Super Bubsy's presentation.  Oh, there is an option to lower the amount of one-liners he utters.
Thing is, I can't mark this as a recommendation. It's by no means a bad game, but I feel disappointed that it doesn't include some of the ideas of the first bubsy game (doorways, more unique enemies, kind of underrated music). For the asking price it doesn't warrant the level of content. Technically this is what one would expect of a Shareware game (e.g. Jazz Jackrabbit 2). This is the amount of content from an Episodic game series (which would be fine if the price weren't what it is). At least if Free DLC or further levels were promised I would be satisfied enough to give a positive review. However as it stands, I feel this falls short compared to the first game. Better than Bubsy 2 and 3D (probably Fractured Tales though haven't seen much of it), but that's not saying too much.

Bubsy: The Woolies Strike Back doesn't inovate enough or differentiate enough from the original games to really stand out. It's pretty much Bubsy except with 2 new moves and a 2.5d perspective. If your thinking about buying this game then I will ask you this, did you like the original games? If yes then thats pretty much what your getting. If you didn't like them then there is no possible way I could reccomend this game to you especially at the retail $30. It has all the problems the originals had (Bubsy dies too easily, poor hitboxes, and repetitive level design) and add's practically nothing.
The game looks OK but lacks forground detail and re-uses textures a lot. The enemy variety is insanely minimal. The soundtrack is ok at times but it's the same song throughout the entirity of a world which gets super annoying. The drawing/animation cutscenes don't look that great either. Bubsy's voice actor is good and the one liners are good but their is so few lines in the game that you'll be hearing the same ones over and over and over again. Did you know that Bubsy doesn't know how he can glide? Me neither, good thing he told me that 50 times already. Bubsy also tends to slide a lot making tight platforming annoying. Each level is practically the same thing with a bunch of copy pasted enemy, and ton of yarn balls, and 5 keys to find to get more yarn balls. He only has ONE power up from what I have seen which allows him to get hit twice before he dies instead of once...... The boss fights can also bee annoying as they don't allow for much movement and attacks can be a little too sudden. It also doesn't help that if you get hit once your sent back up to the top. (Luckily damage is saved).
Overall Bubsy: The Wollies Strike Back! doesn't feel finished and is a poor attempt to revive gamings favorite Bobcat. Despite a great marketing campaign this game just fails as a platformer and pales in comparrison to other 2d platformers that came out this year. Do yourself a favor and if you have not already buy either Sonic Mania $20, Hollow Knight $15, Cuphead $20, or Shovel Knight: Tresure Trove $25 if you want to quench your 2D platformer fix. All of those games came out this year and are fantastic. Don't waste $30 on this, either wait for a price drop or maybe a update that actually adds something to the game. I give Bubsy : The Wollies Strike Back! a 4.2/10 -Infinite

This game passed under my radar when it first came out, but it caught my eye during the fall steam sale this year and I picked it up for about $25.
WORTH. EVERY. PENNY.
If youre looking for a good souls-like game with a bit of a twist go no further. Honestly I would even consider paying full price for this game, but at a (current) sale price of $20 thats a freaking steal.
I'd watched playthroughs of Deck13's previous souls-like game Lords Of The Fallen and some things fell just short of the mark in some places. They must have learned a great deal from this experience though because this game just WORKS.
This'll be a longer review so I'll break it into sections about gameplay and mechanics and then follow with the overall pros/cons...
Combat:
As a souls-like game, I feel like this game hits the mark JUST right. While it may seem easier to some more experienced souls players, combat in this game is still relatively difficult but doesnt make a point to be overtly so. This is one of the areas I feel this game EXCELLS at, even over the souls games. Every time I died to an enemy in this game it actually felt like it was 100% MY fault, unlike many experiences in the souls games where sometimes combat deaths just felt random or unjustified. Boss combat, while still difficult, is significantly more forgiving than most souls games IMO. On average most bosses took 3-7 tries compared to my 8-15 on my first playthrough of dark souls. I feel like this made the game a bit more enjoyable and didnt feel like a complete time sink where I had to put aside a ton of time just to MAYBE beat the boss, and then have to spend 4 tries just refreshing myself when I came back at a later time (Im looking at you nameless king). So in that respect the game is a bit more "casual" and way easier to just pick up and start playing without 10-15 minutes of warmup, which I think is a good thing. But for players who are looking for even more of a challenge from the boss fights, there are also "hardcore" kills for each boss, which are difficult to accomplish but grant increased rewards and special loot. Plus the limb chopping combo finishers are satisfying as ♥♥♥♥ and literally NEVER get old.
Character Building/Progression:
Building your loadout in this game is based off of 4 main aspects: weapons, gear, implants, and core power. Weapons can be swapped freely, with no stat requirements, but sticking with one type of weapon class for some time will increase your proficiency for that class and grant increased damage based on proficiency scaling. Gear is basically your armor. At the begining of the game you start with a very limited selection, but you can expand your gear selection by chopping off the body parts of enemies wearing armor you don't already have (same with weapons). Gear peices can be mixed and matched to create the best combination of stat increases to fit your playstyle or worn as a complete set for a set bonus. Implants are basically chips that you can install into your exo for passive and/or active bonuses like medkits or passive stamina increaseses to even more complex applications. Both gear and implants have a power draw associated with them, and this is where core power comes into play. Core power acts as the limiting factor to your gear and implants, and is basically your level, which you increase in a similar fashion to the souls games by spending your hard earned Tech Scrap (souls). By increasing your core power you are raising the maximum amount of implants and quality gear you can equip.
Overall this progression system is super intuitive, and great for gameplay as you can freely tailor your build to each encounter as you play through the game. While this system does remove some of the replayability, I found it to be much more entertaining because I was able to try out any combination I wanted on the fly and could easily change from a tanky brawler to a fleet footed striker depending on the situation. This also means that The Surge is much more acessable than most of the souls games, requiring much less time consumption and min maxing to create the "perfect" build. Again this feeds into the sense that while difficult, this game is much easier to just pick up and play compared to the souls games.
Graphics&Audio:
Graphics are freaking amazing. Enough said. Plus I was able to max ALL stats and still keep 60 FPS with the GTX1050 in my laptop as well. Audio is amazing, the combat sounds are just so satisfying. Voice acting is wonderful as well, while conversations are few and far between, the voices from the NPCs and recordings did well to add to my immersion overall.
Endgame:
After beating the game for the first time you unlock NG+ which is acesseed by loading your old save after the end credits. This is actually the biggest problem I had with the game, after I beat it the first time I still wanted to go back and explore some more after beating the final boss, but instead I was forced back to the start of the game to replay it again. So make sure you do everything you want BEFORE beating the final boss. With that said, NG+ is JUST as entertaining as the first playthrough. You replay the game from the beginning and keep all your gear from the previous playthrough, with an increase to the gear and weapon upgrade cap. NG+ offers a MUCH higher level of difficulty in the form of much tougher, and SMARTER enemies, as well as the addition of new super strong♥♥♥♥♥beating super enemies scattered throughout the game armed with rare weapons and armor. In this respect the NG+ offers a much more satisfying experience for players who found the base game too easy, while still keeping the satsifying feeling of fair combat.
Overall Pros:
-Freaking great and FAIR combat mechanics
-Mixing and matching gear and collecting sets is fun as hell
-Audio&Visuals 10/10
-Provides a challenging experience but is still easy to pick up/put down any time
-Chopping off peoples arms is satisfying as ♥♥♥♥
-Badass mecha-man
-You work for alternate reality Elon Musk
-Deadmau5 confirmed super hero of the future?
Overall Cons:
-Ambiguous storytelling (some people like this type of thing but I didn't like it in the souls games and I still dont really like it here...)
-Forced into NG+ and can't return to end of game save after beating final boss
-not as many areas as I would have liked, wished for more & larger areas to explore
-numberous shortcuts and paths around the maps felt mazelike at times and occasionally confusing (probably trying to make the most of the smaller areas and limited maps, but sometimes I just wanted a straightforward path...)
-I've become addicted to chopping off peoples lilmbs with futuristic industrial power tools
TL;DR- Buy this game its♥♥♥♥♥♥♥good m8

What do I say about this game that hasn't been already mentioned....
Well, first of all, I didn't use to be an indie game fan, but this game caught my eye, so I gave it try. Oh boy let me tell you, this is more than a game, this is a masterpiece!
The environment, the story, the characters, the gameplay.... it all fits together masterfully. You fall in love with the protagonist as you battle through the robotic menace, struggling to find out what happened to her and how she ended up where she is. The game keeps your mind jumbling as to what the story really holds till the very end, where you have that moment of clarity, and it sure as heck is satisfying. As you progress, you get to meet new characters and learn about them as you read through the functions. Movement and combat are fluid and seemless, and attention has been directed towards every detail.
What else can I say...oh yeah the soundtrack...is one of the best I've ever heard. Truely amazing. Never a dull moment, especially with those humorous one-liners from your transistor companion. If you're worried about replayability, let me tell you, the game makes each replay harder than the previous one, so there's definitely value there. Still finding combat easy? Well, turn on a few limiters, and you'll wish you had activated that last checkpoint.
I cannot recommend this game enough. It needs even more recognition than it currently has.

This battle system is AMAZING. I had played a game with such a battle system (a platformer with a ninja or something though i don't remember the name - that game however was poorly made) and i was wondering why such a battle system was never implemented anywhere else. To all that read this review, i have to tell you what i mean by that: you plan your moves beforehand and the character excecutes them all in some sort of bullet-time event. I have to say this because i didn't know it personally, i only got the game because of the positive reviews and the sci fi feel (i love sci fi rpgs).
This game is artistic, which means that its largest advantage is its scenario/atmosphere. What an amazing feeling. The sword speaks the words that the protagonist can't, while sensual/sad music (similar to portishead) plays in the background. This whole "noir" story develops while you try to find answers by advancing, installing new functions or upgrades, using new limiters. And every time the sword speaks about what you're reading and what you're doing complimenting the already excellent reading material. The story never gets boring and you never need to "grind" (the tests cannot be considered "grinding" since they are one-timers). What you need is to get better and plan more strategically.
The functions (skills) are all different and can all be used as active,passive or to even upgrade other functions and then can be rearranged for different results. (What do i mean by that, let's give a simple example: you have a skill that strikes for some damage. You have a skill that seeks the enemy and does dot. So if you upgrade the first skill with the second skill then the first skill also does dot by itself.)
What can i say? Noir atmosphere, amazing music, captivating story, excellent combat system, diverse skills, without grinding or asking for more money, this game has everything. I bought it on sale but it's really worth its money anyway. I've never finished a game to then be as excited to replay it.
So we've covered the positives. The negatives are very few but there are some.
First of all, at some battles if your character remains at a specific corner the enemies won't chase her (this happened three times, and it's ok in the normal battles since you will eventually have to defeat them so it doesn't really matter, but it also happened during a survival test - i passed the test by positioning my char at a corner that noone could see her).
Secondly at some battles you don't know it but you won't get xp for finishing them (the game wants you (and even tells you) to skip them but if you do them anyway you aren't rewarded) - i would prefer those to be "properly" unbeatable, as if the enemy has a specific armor that you can't remove and which negates all damage or that the enemy is completely untargettable. This happened only twice in the game (and actually you already kind of know that you won't get any xp but you try anyway).
Thirdly in some cases the sword was talking because of the storyline progression and as he was talking i pressed to observe something and i basically lost the dialogue for what i was observing. I felt that twice or three times towards the end.
Fourth, in some cases the game would not play that well, as if it was overwhelmed with graphics. I don't know if that makes much sense. Although my graphics card is obviously not the best, it does cover a lot more than the minimum requirements but i still got some cases of "laggy" instances. By that i mean that the world did not feel as smooth as in other areas. This happened frequently but it's mostly due to my graphics card i guess.
In these "negatives" i specifically said how many times it happened because i wanted the readers to know that even these happen once or twice in the entire game. The game is almost literally a masterpiece. It's like reading a book but you're actually playing it. It's awesome. I honestly didn't expect this to be that good. But it is.
So my advice to all of you who are even mildly interested is to buy it straight away. It is a finished game that has a lot of replayability and never feels buggy or unfinished or boring. And right now it's up for sale for 4 euros, it's silly not to get it. But it's even worth its original price of 19 euros.

The surge is a hardcore rpg that aims to borrow all of the good parts of Lords of the Fallen and Dark Souls.
The gameplay mechanics around movement seems to be an exact blend between the two.  It has the weight and feel of the larger weapons in LOTF and most of the strategy of dark souls.

You will be darting back and forth, in and out, but mostly estimating the impact of your weapons against the stability of your enemies in order to deal the most damage per combo.

Graphics, 9/10
Runs perfectly on max settings on a gtx 970 with a reasonable i5.
I was quite impressed on how they handled the background loading and transitions between areas. It's not flashy but it works quickly and efficiently. Also loading into an area that you have already been to is almost instant, a huge thank-you to the developers for keeping the majority of the assets loaded to facilitate this.  - there is a current glitch with the position of the first security gear set after some animations that cause it to appear slightly behind you.

Gameplay 9/10
There are a few conceptual flaws here, but none relating to it's implementation.
When killing an enemy with a finisher off a ledge both the item and yourself will remain at the position to which the finisher started.
Darting in and out as people keep complaining about is partially correct as yes it works the majority of the time, but it is slower, less efficient, not possible late game (excluding the last boss which NEEDS to be completely reworked) and not fun.  Putting it plainly, the combat around this game benefits from simply being COOL.  I found the staff to be the most viable weapon by far, but that might just be personal preference.  I do enjoy slower and larger weapons but they have this annoying mini-hit in between large swings that does nothing but expose you to being pummeled (This may be intentional).  When using a larger weapon i want to take advantage of the huge impact rating, this mini-hit (until the black Cerberus) prevents this.

Level design 5/10
Oh my god some of these levels are moronic.  Dark souls has a complex level design set in a similar manner, but it was done so in a way that granted a player great spacial awareness.  This was done using open areas and the ability to look over the entire city from several locations.  It does not work in closed spaces with tight and windy walkways.
The amount of bloody corners that have an enemy waiting for you thankfully reduces as you progress later into the game.  There are in-game signs (no fkn map) to assist you in getting where you need to go, but no painted floor lines like the ones found in some manufacturing facilities (which would have been a great idea). The site maps that are present are basically useless and completely void of useful information and this is assuming that you see them at all.
Honestly, if they present the player more information the level design would improve drastically, i get that they want you to explore but there needs to be better indication on where to go, or it's not exploring, it's just wandering about until you think you found that path you are meant to travel.    - Ask NPCs where to go, they actually give useful information.
There needs to be a fast travel system that unlocks just before the last boss and only just before the last boss.


Overall this still gets an 8/10 due to the relative impact of each category including the ones not commented on in this review.  It is an excellent game that is quite underrated.  I was actually quite astounded at how long i could play this in one sitting completely entertained.

I wouldn't call this game "hard" as lots of reviewers seem to, but I would definitely call it "unforgiving".  It reminds me a lot of my WoW days.  Learn the levels, pull the right enemies at the right times and your life is easy-going.  But when it goes wrong, or that patrol you didn't see hits you, then it layers on the stress but is very rewarding.
The content is also really fun with lots of large areas to explore and learn the layouts, finding all the goodies hidden away (I would recommend playing the first map and if you enjoy it then pick up the DLC with the scanner in it as it's vital to find all the best goodies - you can re-scan through the first map to find anything you missed after picking up the DLC).
Enemy variety is good and bosses are exceptionally brutal, with one-hit-kills abound.
Combat is extremely satisfying, with each weapon feeling different levels of impact, sound effects and gore are all there to add to the show.  There is a meaningful choice between using different armour sets and weapons.  You can block low-impact weapons then counter-attack, or dodge high-impact weapons so they don't knock you over, then hit the enemy while they are off-balance.  Because the combat is reaction-based some may find it overwhelming but it's possible to build around heavy armour and blocking more than dodging with enough HP and Regen implants.
Overall the game has a surprising amount of depth and replayability, I'm looking forward starting a New Game + after I complete my initial playthrough!

My past with Eugen Systems is a very positive one. They were actually the ones who manage to release Act of War: Direct Action, a game reminiscent of C&C Generals but better in all aspects. They then did their first game with their Iriszoom engine called R.U.S.E. a magnificent game where you still built bases and played around with decoys to confuse your opponent about where you`re actual troops where massing. An interesting idea but it sort of went under the radar despite being a Ubisoft game. The Wargame series is where Eugen Systems first truelly epic contribution to the tactical RTS genre. Releasing a game which looks on the surface like "World In Conflict" Cold War going hot kind of game, but it has extreme realism and a pretty accurate depiction of tactics, weapons and units. I started playing the series with Wargame: Airland Battle extensively until Red Dragon came out and is probably one of the few who would argue that Airland Battle is the best in Wargame series. These games where released by Focus Home Interactive and I think it pretty much explains why Eugen Systems haven`t been noticed for their games. In comes Paradox Interactive and teams up with Eugen!
[Another Wargame, but better!]
Steel Division: Normandy 44 is Eugen Systems first team up with Paradox. The game is probably whaqt many R.U.S.E and Wargame fans had been waiting for, a Eugen game set up in World War 2. And if you have played Wargame, the concept is pretty much the same. Compose a battlegroup and go into action either in skirmish or on multiplayer, or play through a short campaign describing the Normandy campaign from american, german and british perspectives.
News for this time is that battles have been set up in three phases, were units are assigned to each phase. This is pretty much designed for small skirmishes in the beginning to escalate into proper chaos in mid late game. The game is very much about the tactics of warfare. Instead of having to capture points on a map like in Wargame, you mainly see just a moving frontline and holding as much of the map as possible guarantee a win, and depending on how much you hold, the more victory points are earned.
The trick is that you are unaware of what caused the frontline to move, and what hides behind the fog of war and the same goes for your opponent. You can use scout aircraft or scouts on the ground to locate enemies and get an understanding of what opposition you are facing. But the lack of knowing what the enemies is throwing at you and from what direction makes this game feel a bit like R.U.S.E. when you used decoys. If you use this well you can get an advantage that takes some real effort from the opponent in order to dislodge you.
Another big difference from Wargame is that confrontations are on a smaller scale. You no longer mass up a lot of tanks, infantry etc in one big group from deployment and give them orders. This time around microing units is key to success. And where you place individual units is very important. For example I had a scout in the right place during my first multiplayer session which allowed me to gain a good understanding of the composition of an armoured column heading my my way. Another example is when I had sneaked up a konigstiger behind a tree line and awaited an attack move by the Konigstiger in at a barn I was holding. I was able to flank and destroy 10-15 tanks and armoured transports with that single tank.
Multiplayer and skirmish is very much recognisable from the Wargame series. However the Singleplayer campaign could have been done better. There is no tactical map, or any dynamic campaign in the style of those in Wargame: Airland Battle or in that of Red Dragon. It`s a linear map of different battles fought in Normandy campaign. It`s a good introduction to Steel Division`s other features but to be honest I did expect something more.
Steel Division is an excellent game! It`s hailed among the reviewers and that is for a good reason, namely that this is as close you`ll get to have a realistic WW2 tactical RTS with good graphics and good emersion. Under Paradox flag, I`m excited to see where thay are takiong this rebranded Wargame next. A new series perhaps? Perhaps visiting the Eastern Front of World War 2? Korea? Vietnam? I`m just genuinely looking forward to Eugen Systems bright new future with Paradox! It`s a strong 9/10. A more engaging Singleplayer campaign would have pushed it over to a 10/10

Before I write anything let me first establish that I am not a fan of fighting games, this is the first "traditional" fighitng game that I've ever played more than a few matches in. I'd also like to point out that, as I don't own a controller, I played with a keyboard, this makes the controlls significantly more challenging for me. However, I still love this game.
Pros:
-Combos are surpisingly not that hard for me to pull off. Although I do have issues with some.
-Combat feels very fluid even though I often am not sure what I'm doing.
-Multiple different fighting modes. So, even if you're scared of going online because you might face someone who actually knows what they're doing, like me, there's still plenty to play.
-I can tell that each character is unique with their own personality and backstory, at least with the characters that I played.
-The backgrounds to the stages are absolutely beautiful.
Cons:
-There seems to only be one major flaw with this game, aside from those inherit to the fighting genre. The story mode is so confusing. I don't mean that the story is confusing, although it certainly is with my lack of understanding of the characters  and the previous stories. What I mean is that, I honestly learned more of the story from the arcade mode then the story mode and no matter what matches I win in the story mode, it always seems to end in the failure screen. This is most likely an issue with something that I'm doing but it's still very confusing.
Overall, I'd recommend this game to fighter fans and non-fighter fans alike.

Positive:
+ a lot of possibilities to design your factory
+ a lot of fun building, researching, surviving
+ quite decent developing, it's not dead by developer side [actually the updates bring often new interesting features]
+ you have the option that aliens only attack when you initiate combat (beginner friendly)
+ map editor
+ seeds available
+ you can use napalm to destroy aliens
Negative:
- late game motivation is only how many satellites can you shoot

- not a suitibale game for everyone

having played FFXIV in its original incarnation, a realm reborn rebuilt everything from the ground up and is now currently one of the top MMORPGS in the world. The game its self is very story led which helps you level your initial class choice, and then side quests,dungeons, fun side events etc all help you level additional jobs. You dont need to create a seperate character for each class/job you try out, you merely equip your weapon of choice and off you go.
So you have 4 main job categories - Disciples of War and Magic, this is your melee, tank and spellcaster classes and Disciples of the Land/Hand which is your gathering and crafting classes. It  is possible to play entirely how you want.
Being Final Fantasy the story is epic, and the story is a joy to experience (DONT USE A JUMP POTION UNLESS YOUR LEVELLING A SECOND CHARACTER)
Lip service is paid to previous Final Fantasy's with previous bosses, characters and monsters all making appearances. Chocobo's - check, Moogles - Check - Tonberries - Check!
The Gold Saucer from FFVII makes an appearance and is a good way to play lots of mini games within the game, you can chocob race, play Triple Triad from FFVIII and a host of other activities.
Its not a game you can dip in and out of, it does require some dedication, especially when you reach the current level cap and start the long grind towards gearing up but it never really becomes a chore.
On the whole FFXIV is a well rounded, very enjoyable MMORPG. It does have a cash shop, but this is purely for cosmetic items and by no means a pay to win measure.
My only critisism would be not enough is done to help new players learn basic mechanics, yes theres Hall of the Novice, but youd have to seek it out to know it was there. Hall of The Novice should be made to include the first dungeon to introduce people to team work and how their classes synergise. There is a mentor system but at present it seems to be very one sided, people become mentors purely because on completion of a set amount of mentor dungeons you get an exlusive mount, very few people actually take their mentor roles seriously (However on my server - Moggle, the mentors there are on the whole pretty decent!)
The game is quite slow to begin with again which is not a critisism but may put some people off, but the learning curve is necessary.
For me, this actually beats WoW! not many games can have that claim to fame in this genre!

BUBSY! YOU'RE BACK! A little short, but YOU'RE NOT TERRIBLE!
Bubsy's newest installment "The Woolies Strike Back" had me a bit worried it would be a pile of garbage like the previous game Bubsy 3D and the original Bubsy 1 and 2, but, alas, it's good.
The music is not bad, the game functions well (only crashed once so far, and I was kind of disappointed that happened, but I carried on). The graphics are fine, a tad bit un-inspired, but its good.
Now, I will be honest, and I will admit, this is NOT on the same level of greatness like Sonic Mania or Super Mario Odyssey, but when comparing it to the older Bubsy games, it's day and night!
In Bubsy 1 and 2, they had levels designed like they were based off Mario games, but Bubsy had this issue of being able to run way too fast, easily making Bubsy run into enemies that would be impossible to avoid, killing Bubsy, and therefore making the levels way too hard and frustrating. One hit deaths made the already annoying games difficult, and even with 9 lives (get it? Because he's a cat?), the games were still relentless and just not fun. The level design was all over the place, and the sense of flow was just nonexistent. There was so many things trying to kill Bubsy and it was hard to get through even just the first level. They even had falling damage! Yes, in Bubsy 1 and 2, you could die if you feel from too far a height! Sometimes it's not even that far up and you STILL die!
The Woolies Strike Back, however, it is almost the total opposite. I swear each level became more and more fun and well thought out (still have not beaten the game, but I'm past halfway I think). The controls feel great and respond well, and there's a good amount of competency in the design of some of the parts where you need just a bit of puzzle solving skills to figure out what's the best way around some parts.
Yes, there are some spots in a few of the levels that were a bit frustrating, but they never got horrendous, not even close to the abomination of the older Bubsy games. The worst part so far might have been on the first (or second) level where there was a small body of water in a tight cave-like space, and you need to jump through this rock barricade to land across the water. So, I use Bubsy's weird pounce attack (X on the Xbox controller), and I smash through the rock, but I end up falling right into the water and died! Like 3 times in a row! On my 4th try I got it, but the good news is the game never becomes as frustrating as that part ever again. I think the boss fights are okay, not awful, but not amazing. I don't really know how to explain it, ya know?
You still have one-hit deaths and the 9 lives, BUT, in its defense, it's not as easy to die in this game as it is in Bubsy 1 and 2, therefore the game feels less relentless. If you pick up a black T-Shirt powerup, it gives Bubsy a onetime use shield which is useful. And, if you pick up another black T-Shirt while wearing one, it'll give Bubsy an extra life, and I personally find that very unique. Also, a fun little extra is that you can use the Right stick on a controller to pan the camera a bit vertically and/or horizontally in case you need to see past the camera, and this works well actually, I really appreciate this feature.
So, Bubsy is back. He's not 100% amazing, but I think The Woolies Strike Back is totally worth a playthrough, what could possibly go wrong? Get it while it's on sale, I kind of feel like $30 is a bit much to ask for a Bubsy game.
Also, the pause menu music is sick, and I really don't know why lol.
